effects.quote: When administered to pregnant women, androgens cause virilization of the external genitalia of the female fetus. This virilization includes clitoromegaly, abnormal vaginal development, and fusion of genital folds to form a scrotal-like structure.
effects.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

other_effects.text: In animal studies, the US Xyosted label says testosterone exposure in the womb caused hormonal and behavioural changes in offspring as well as structural impairments of reproductive tissues in both sexes.
other_effects.quote: In animal developmental studies, exposure to testosterone in utero resulted in hormonal and behavioral changes in offspring and structural impairments of reproductive tissues in female and male offspring.
other_effects.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

paternal.text: France's ANSM says pregnant women must avoid all contact with testosterone gel application sites, and a man whose partner is pregnant must be especially careful with the precautions against transfer.
paternal.quote: Les femmes enceintes doivent éviter tout contact avec les sites d'application de ce médicament. En cas de grossesse chez sa partenaire, le patient devra être d'autant plus vigilant quant aux précautions d'utilisation
paternal.source_label: ANSM, Androgel 50 mg gel transdermique en sachet-dose, RCP section 4.4 (Transfert peau à peau)

monitoring.text: The US label says a patient who becomes pregnant while taking androgens should be told of the potential hazard to the fetus, and it names no specific prenatal test or newborn check.
monitoring.quote: If the patient becomes pregnant while taking androgens, she should be apprised of the potential hazard to the fetus.
monitoring.source_label: US label, Testosterone Enanthate injection, Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA, Contraindications, via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The Xyosted label bases the statement that testosterone is teratogenic on animal data and its mechanism of action, and it gives no count of exposed human pregnancies.
evidence_base.quote: Testosterone is teratogenic and may cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman based on data from animal studies and its mechanism of action
evidence_base.source_label: US label, Xyosted (testosterone enanthate) injection, Antares Pharma, section 8.1 Pregnancy, via openFDA

regulatory.text: The US boxed warning for oral ribavirin contraindicates it in pregnant women and in the male partners of pregnant women, citing teratogenic and embryocidal effects in all animal species.
regulatory.quote: Therefore, ribavirin therapy is contraindicated in women who are pregnant and in the male partners of women who are pregnant.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, Boxed Warning

dose.text: In animal studies, ribavirin was teratogenic and embryocidal at doses as low as one twentieth of the recommended human dose, and effects increased with dose.
dose.quote: These effects occurred at doses as low as one twentieth of the recommended human dose of ribavirin.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, section 5.1 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity and section 8.1 Animal Data

effects.text: In animal studies only, ribavirin caused malformations of the skull, palate, eye, jaw, limbs, skeleton and gastrointestinal tract; the human registry showed no pattern of birth defects.
effects.quote: Malformations of the skull, palate, eye, jaw, limbs, skeleton, and gastrointestinal tract were noted.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data and Human Data)

other_effects.text: The US label reports reduced survival of fetuses and offspring in animals, and an approximately 21% miscarriage rate in the registry, which it calls insufficient to identify a drug risk.
other_effects.quote: The miscarriage rate was approximately 21%.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy

absolute_risk.text: The US label reports birth defects in 9.09% of 88 live births after direct exposure and 6.12% of 98 after exposure through a male partner, versus a 2.72% MACDP background rate.
absolute_risk.quote: show a higher rate of birth defects (9.09% and 6.12%, respectively) compared to a background birth defect rate of 2.72% in the Metropolitan Atlanta Congenital Defects Program (MACDP) birth defects surveillance system
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Human Data (Ribavirin Pregnancy Registry)

before_after.text: The US label says ribavirin should not be started until a negative pregnancy test is obtained immediately before starting, and calls for effective contraception with periodic pregnancy tests during treatment and for 9 months after stopping, in female patients.
before_after.quote: Female patients should use effective contraception and have periodic monitoring with pregnancy tests during treatment and during the 9-month period after treatment has been stopped.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, section 5.1 Embryo-Fetal Toxicity

paternal.text: The US label contraindicates ribavirin in men whose female partners are pregnant and tells male patients and their female partners to use contraception during treatment and for 6 months after.
paternal.quote: Male patients and their female partners should use effective contraception during treatment and during the 6-month period after treatment has been stopped.
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, ribavirin capsules (Aurobindo Pharma), effective 6 February 2024, read via openFDA, section 4 Contraindications and section 5.1

monitoring.text: Health Canada requires routine monthly pregnancy tests during therapy and tells patients to inform their physician immediately if a pregnancy is detected.
monitoring.quote: During therapy, routine monthly pregnancy tests must be performed, and patients should be advised to tell their physician immediately if a pregnancy is detected.
monitoring.source_label: Health Canada, IBAVYR (ribavirin tablets) Product Monograph, revised 15 March 2022, section 7.1.1 Pregnant Women

evidence_base.text: The Ribavirin Pregnancy Registry (2004-2020) enrolled 280 pregnancies exposed to oral ribavirin directly or through a male partner, with 186 live births, and did not meet its sample size.
evidence_base.quote: The registry enrolled 280 pregnancies resulting in 186 live births
evidence_base.source_label: Sinclair SM et al., Final results from the ribavirin pregnancy registry, 2004-2020, Birth Defects Res 2022;114(20):1376-1391, PMID 36305304 (abstract read)

regulatory.text: The EU contraindicates fingolimod during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential not using effective contraception, with a Physician Information Pack and pregnancy-specific patient reminder card.
regulatory.quote: Due to risk to the foetus, fingolimod is contraindicated during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential not using effective contraception.
regulatory.source_label: EMA, Gilenya product information (SmPC), EPAR PDF dated 7 September 2026, sections 4.3, 4.4 and Annex II

window.text: MHRA says that, because of its long half-life, fingolimod taken during the 8 weeks leading up to the last menstrual period may expose a subsequent pregnancy.
window.quote: Due to its long half-life, use of fingolimod during the 8 weeks leading up to the last menstrual period may result in exposure of a subsequent pregnancy.
window.source_label: UK MHRA Drug Safety Update, volume 13 issue 2, 19 September 2019: fingolimod and congenital malformations

dose.text: In rat studies, fingolimod was teratogenic at 0.1 mg/kg or higher, where drug exposure was similar to that of patients on the 0.5 mg therapeutic dose.
dose.quote: Fingolimod was teratogenic in the rat when given at doses of 0.1 mg/kg or higher. Drug exposure in rats at this dose was similar to that in patients at the therapeutic dose (0.5 mg).
dose.source_label: EMA, Gilenya product information (SmPC), EPAR PDF dated 7 September 2026, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data

effects.text: The US label says the most frequent major birth defects in the Gilenya pregnancy registry were congenital heart defects, renal/urinary malformations and limb/musculoskeletal malformations.
effects.quote: The most frequent major birth defects were congenital heart defects, renal/urinary malformations, and limb/musculoskeletal malformations.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Gilenya (Novartis), effective 22 July 2026, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Human Data

other_effects.text: In rats given fingolimod during pregnancy and lactation, pup survival fell at all doses and offspring showed a learning deficit at the high dose (animal data).
other_effects.quote: pup survival was decreased at all doses and a neurobehavioral (learning) deficit was seen in offspring at the high dose
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Gilenya (Novartis), effective 22 July 2026, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data

absolute_risk.text: In the Gilenya pregnancy registry (2011-2024), 8.2% (EUROCAT) or 10.9% (MACDP) of 147 first-trimester-exposed outcomes had major birth defects, against a 2% to 4% US background.
absolute_risk.quote: the rate of major birth defects among 147 live births, stillbirths, or terminations of pregnancy due to fetal anomalies from women who were administered fingolimod during the first trimester was 8.2% (95% CI: 4.3-13.8)
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Gilenya (Novartis), effective 22 July 2026, read via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Human Data (Gilenya Pregnancy Registry 2011-2024)

before_after.text: EU product information requires a negative pregnancy test before starting, effective contraception during treatment and for 2 months after stopping, and stopping fingolimod 2 months before planning a pregnancy.
before_after.quote: Women of childbearing potential must use effective contraception during treatment and for 2 months after discontinuation of Gilenya, since fingolimod takes approximately 2 months to eliminate from the body after treatment discontinuation
before_after.source_label: EMA, Gilenya product information (SmPC), EPAR PDF dated 7 September 2026, sections 4.4 and 4.6

paternal.text: Health Canada says available data do not suggest that fingolimod is associated with an increased risk of male-mediated fetal toxicity.
paternal.quote: Available data do not suggest that GILENYA would be associated with an increased risk of male-mediated fetal toxicity.
paternal.source_label: Health Canada, GILENYA Product Monograph (Novartis), authorized 2 September 2026, section 7 Reproductive Health, Male Reproductive Toxicity

monitoring.text: EU product information says to stop fingolimod if a woman becomes pregnant, give medical advice on the fetal risk, and perform ultrasonography examinations.
monitoring.quote: Medical advice should be given regarding the risk of harmful effects to the foetus associated with treatment and ultrasonography examinations should be performed.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Gilenya product information (SmPC), EPAR PDF dated 7 September 2026, section 4.6 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: The 2019 EU review that found a two-fold malformation risk used post-marketing data, including registry data, with prospective data from 1,465 women exposed to fingolimod during pregnancy.
evidence_base.quote: Prospective data were included from 1,465 women exposed to fingolimod during pregnancy.
evidence_base.source_label: UK MHRA Drug Safety Update, volume 13 issue 2, 19 September 2019: fingolimod and congenital malformations, Background

regulatory.text: The EU label contraindicates pomalidomide in pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential unless all conditions of the pregnancy prevention programme are met.
regulatory.quote: Pomalidomide is contraindicated during pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential, except when all the conditions for pregnancy prevention have been met (see sections 4.3 and 4.4).
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.6 Pregnancy

window.text: In animal studies, pomalidomide was teratogenic in rats and rabbits when given during the period of major organogenesis.
window.quote: Pomalidomide was found to be teratogenic in both rats and rabbits when administered during the period of major organogenesis.
window.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

dose.text: In rabbits, the developmental no-observed-adverse-effect level lay below 10 mg/kg/day, the lowest dose tested, whose exposure was similar to that from a 4 mg clinical dose.
dose.quote: the developmental NOAEL was < 10 mg/kg/day (AUC24h was 418 ng•h/mL on Gestation Day 19 at this lowest dose tested, which was similar to that obtained from a 4 mg clinical dose)
dose.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

effects.text: In animal studies, pomalidomide caused limb anomalies with unattached or absent digits in rabbits at 250 mg/kg/day, and absent bladder and thyroid in rats at all doses tested.
effects.quote: At 250 mg/kg/day, fetal malformations included limb anomalies (flexed and/or rotated fore- and/or hindlimbs, unattached or absent digit) and associated skeletal malformations
effects.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

other_effects.text: In rabbits, pomalidomide at 100 and 250 mg/kg/day slightly increased post-implantation loss and slightly decreased fetal body weights.
other_effects.quote: At 100 and 250 mg/kg/day, there were slight increases in post-implantation loss and slight decreases in fetal body weights.
other_effects.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Embryo-foetal development

before_after.text: The EU label requires women of childbearing potential to use effective contraception without interruption from at least 4 weeks before treatment until at least 4 weeks after it ends.
before_after.quote: She understands the need for effective contraception, without interruption, at least 4 weeks before starting treatment, throughout the entire duration of treatment, and at least 4 weeks after the end of treatment
before_after.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.4 Special warnings, Counselling

paternal.text: As a precaution, the EU label asks men taking pomalidomide to use condoms during treatment, dose interruptions and for 7 days after stopping if the partner is pregnant, or fertile without contraception.
paternal.quote: As a precaution, all male patients taking pomalidomide should use condoms throughout treatment duration, during dose interruption and for 7 days after cessation of treatment if their partner is pregnant or of childbearing potential and has no contraception
paternal.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.6 Contraception in males and females

monitoring.text: If a treated woman becomes pregnant, the EU label says to stop treatment and refer her to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs in a woman treated with pomalidomide, treatment must be stopped and the patient should be referred to a physician specialised or experienced in teratology for evaluation and advice.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information Imnovid (pomalidomide), SmPC, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: The US label bases its embryo-fetal harm warning on pomalidomide's mechanism of action and on findings from animal studies.
evidence_base.quote: Based on the mechanism of action [see Clinical Pharmacology (12.1) ] and findings from animal studies, POMALYST can cause embryo-fetal harm when administered to a pregnant female and is contraindicated during pregnancy
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label Pomalyst (pomalidomide), via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary

regulatory.text: The EU label contraindicates vismodegib in pregnancy and in women of childbearing potential who do not comply with the Erivedge Pregnancy Prevention Programme.
regulatory.quote: Erivedge is contraindicated in WCBP who do not comply with the Erivedge Pregnancy Prevention Programme.
regulatory.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, sections 4.3 Contraindications and 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

window.text: EU assessors expect vismodegib to cause pronounced fetal toxicity throughout pregnancy, given its strong teratogenic potential and the likely importance of hedgehog signalling in later developmental stages.
window.quote: Based on the strong teratogenic potential, and the likely importance of hedgehog signalling also in later developmental stages, vismodegib is expected to exhibit pronounced foetal toxicity throughout the pregnancy
window.source_label: EMA CHMP assessment report Erivedge (vismodegib), non-clinical discussion

dose.text: In rats, the lowest dose tested, 10 mg/kg/day, about 0.2 times human exposure at 150 mg, caused malformations, and doses of 60 mg/kg/day or more caused early resorption of all fetuses.
dose.quote: A dose of 10 mg/kg/day [approximately 0.2 times the human exposure (AUC) at the recommended 150 mg clinical dose] resulted in malformations (including missing and/or fused digits, open perineum and craniofacial anomalies)
dose.source_label: US FDA label Erivedge (vismodegib), via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Animal Data

effects.text: In animal species, hedgehog pathway inhibitors such as vismodegib were embryotoxic or teratogenic and can cause severe malformations, including craniofacial anomalies, midline defects and limb defects.
effects.quote: Hedgehog pathway inhibitors (see section 5.1) such as vismodegib, have been demonstrated to be embryotoxic and/or teratogenic in multiple animal species and can cause severe malformations, including craniofacial anomalies, midline defects and limb defects
effects.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.6 Pregnancy

other_effects.text: The EU label says irreversible tooth defects and premature growth-plate closure, seen in rat toxicity studies at clinically relevant exposures, represent risks to post-natal development; no dedicated post-natal study was done.
other_effects.quote: irreversible defects in growing teeth and premature closure of the femoral epiphyseal plate, observed in rat toxicity studies at clinically relevant exposures, represent risks to post-natal development
other_effects.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data, Post-natal development

before_after.text: Women of childbearing potential must use two methods, one highly effective plus a barrier, during treatment and for 24 months after the last dose, and test negative within 7 days before starting.
before_after.quote: Female patients must use two methods of recommended contraception including one highly effective method and a barrier method during Erivedge therapy and for 24 months after the final dose
before_after.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.4 Special warnings, Contraception and Pregnancy testing

paternal.text: Because vismodegib is present in semen, the EU label requires men to use a condom, even after vasectomy, during treatment and for 2 months after the final dose.
paternal.quote: male patients must always use a condom (with spermicide, if available), even after a vasectomy, when having sex with a female partner while taking Erivedge
paternal.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.6 Contraception in males and females

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs during treatment, the EU label requires that Erivedge be stopped immediately.
monitoring.quote: In case of pregnancy in a woman treated with Erivedge, treatment must be stopped immediately.
monitoring.source_label: EMA product information Erivedge (vismodegib), SmPC, section 4.6 Pregnancy

evidence_base.text: The US label states that there are no human data on vismodegib use in pregnant women and that a Genentech-run pregnancy exposure registry monitors outcomes.
evidence_base.quote: There are no human data on the use of ERIVEDGE in pregnant women.
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label Erivedge (vismodegib), via openFDA, section 8.1 Pregnancy, Risk Summary

regulatory.text: The US label carries a boxed warning that contraindicates bosentan in pregnancy because, based on animal data, it may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.quote: TRACLEER is contraindicated for use during pregnancy because it may cause fetal harm if used by pregnant females based on animal data.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, Boxed Warning (Embryo-Fetal Toxicity), via openFDA

dose.text: In rats, bosentan caused birth defects at blood levels higher than 1.5 times those reached at the human therapeutic dose.
dose.quote: Bosentan has been shown to be teratogenic in rats at plasma levels higher than 1.5 times the plasma concentrations achieved at the therapeutic dose in humans.
dose.source_label: EMA, Tracleer (bosentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 5.3 Preclinical safety data

effects.text: In a rat study, bosentan caused dose-dependent malformations of the head, mouth, face and large blood vessels.
effects.quote: In an embryo-fetal toxicity study in rats, bosentan showed dose-dependent teratogenic effects, including malformations of the head, mouth, face and large blood vessels.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

other_effects.text: In rats, bosentan increased stillbirths and deaths of newborn pups at oral doses 2 and 10 times the maximum recommended human dose.
other_effects.quote: Bosentan increased stillbirths and pup mortality at oral doses 2 and 10 times the MRHD (on a mg/m 2 basis).
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The US label gives no rate for exposed pregnancies and says data limitations preclude a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes.
absolute_risk.quote: These limitations preclude establishing a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes with maternal ERA use.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

before_after.text: The US label says to exclude pregnancy before starting bosentan and to use effective contraception before starting, during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Females of reproductive potential: Exclude pregnancy before initiating treatment. Use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment and for one month after stopping TRACLEER
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, Boxed Warning (highlights), via openFDA

paternal.text: The US label addresses only male fertility, reporting decreased sperm counts in patients and unknown reversibility, not risk to a pregnancy fathered by a treated man.
paternal.quote: Decreased sperm counts have been observed in patients receiving TRACLEER. Based on these findings and findings in animals, TRACLEER may impair fertility in males of reproductive potential. It is not known whether effects on fertility would be reversible
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.3 Females and Males of Reproductive Potential (Infertility, Males), via openFDA

monitoring.text: EMA recommends monthly pregnancy tests during bosentan treatment for early detection, because hormonal contraception may fail and pregnancy can severely worsen pulmonary hypertension.
monitoring.quote: Because of possible hormonal contraception failure during Tracleer treatment, and also bearing in mind the risk that pulmonary hypertension severely deteriorates with pregnancy, monthly pregnancy tests during treatment with Tracleer are recommended to allow early detection of pregnancy.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Tracleer (bosentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: The human evidence rests on postmarketing reports and published literature from decades of ERA use, which have not identified an increased risk of major birth defects but are limited.
evidence_base.quote: Available data from postmarketing reports and published literature over decades of use with endothelin receptor antagonists (ERA) in the same class as TRACLEER have not identified an increased risk of major birth defects; however, these data are limited.
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, Tracleer (bosentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

regulatory.text: FDA states that endothelin receptor antagonist medicines are contraindicated in pregnancy because animal studies show they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.quote: Use of ERA medicines is contraindicated in pregnancy. Based on data from animal EFT studies, pregnant patients should not use ERA medicines as they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA, Endothelin Receptor Antagonist REMS Information (content current as of 03/04/2026)

dose.text: In animal studies, ambrisentan caused birth defects in rats and rabbits at exposures 3.5 and 1.7 times those of the 10 mg human daily dose, and lower doses were not studied.
dose.quote: In animal reproduction studies, Letairis was teratogenic in rats and rabbits at doses which resulted in exposures of 3.5 and 1.7 times, respectively, the human dose of 10 mg per day
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

effects.text: In rats and rabbits, ambrisentan caused abnormalities of the lower jaw and palate, heart and great-vessel malformations, and failure of the thymus and thyroid to form.
effects.quote: In both species, there were abnormalities of the lower jaw and hard and soft palate, malformation of the heart and great vessels, and failure of formation of the thymus and thyroid.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

other_effects.text: In rats, macitentan given from late pregnancy through lactation reduced pup survival and impaired the male offspring's fertility at all doses tested.
other_effects.quote: Administration of macitentan to female rats from late pregnancy through lactation caused reduced pup survival and impairment of the male fertility of the offspring at all dose levels tested.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Opsumit (macitentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The US label gives no rate for exposed pregnancies and says data limitations preclude a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes.
absolute_risk.quote: These limitations preclude establishing a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes with maternal endothelin receptor antagonist use.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

before_after.text: The US ambrisentan label calls for a pregnancy test before starting and advises effective contraception before starting, during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Obtain a pregnancy test prior to initiation of treatment with Letairis. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for one month after discontinuation of treatment with Letairis.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 5.1 Embryo-fetal Toxicity, via openFDA

paternal.text: The EU macitentan label addresses only male fertility, saying ERAs may harm sperm production in men, not risk to a pregnancy fathered by a treated man.
paternal.quote: Decreases in sperm count have been observed in patients taking ERAs. Macitentan, like other ERAs, may have an adverse effect on spermatogenesis in men.
paternal.source_label: EMA, Opsumit (macitentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 (Male fertility)

monitoring.text: EMA recommends monthly pregnancy tests while a woman of childbearing potential takes ambrisentan.
monitoring.quote: Monthly pregnancy tests during treatment with ambrisentan are recommended.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Volibris (ambrisentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: FDA's 2025 decision rested on human fetal outcomes reported from 2001 to 2024 after exposure to any ERA, which showed no pattern of malformations like those seen in animals.
evidence_base.quote: based on an evaluation of human fetal outcomes reported from 2001 to 2024 after exposure to a drug in the endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) pharmacologic class. These data have not shown a pattern of congenital malformations
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA, supplement approval letter NDA 022081/S-045 (Letairis), removal of the Ambrisentan REMS

regulatory.text: FDA states that endothelin receptor antagonist medicines are contraindicated in pregnancy because animal studies show they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.quote: Use of ERA medicines is contraindicated in pregnancy. Based on data from animal EFT studies, pregnant patients should not use ERA medicines as they may cause fetal harm.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA, Endothelin Receptor Antagonist REMS Information (content current as of 03/04/2026)

dose.text: In animal studies, ambrisentan caused birth defects in rats and rabbits at exposures 3.5 and 1.7 times those of the 10 mg human daily dose, and lower doses were not studied.
dose.quote: In animal reproduction studies, Letairis was teratogenic in rats and rabbits at doses which resulted in exposures of 3.5 and 1.7 times, respectively, the human dose of 10 mg per day
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

effects.text: In rats and rabbits, ambrisentan caused abnormalities of the lower jaw and palate, heart and great-vessel malformations, and failure of the thymus and thyroid to form.
effects.quote: In both species, there were abnormalities of the lower jaw and hard and soft palate, malformation of the heart and great vessels, and failure of formation of the thymus and thyroid.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

other_effects.text: In rats, macitentan given from late pregnancy through lactation reduced pup survival and impaired the male offspring's fertility at all doses tested.
other_effects.quote: Administration of macitentan to female rats from late pregnancy through lactation caused reduced pup survival and impairment of the male fertility of the offspring at all dose levels tested.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Opsumit (macitentan), Actelion Pharmaceuticals US, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Animal Data), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The US label gives no rate for exposed pregnancies and says data limitations preclude a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes.
absolute_risk.quote: These limitations preclude establishing a reliable estimate of the risk of adverse fetal and neonatal outcomes with maternal endothelin receptor antagonist use.
absolute_risk.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 8.1 Pregnancy (Risk Summary), via openFDA

before_after.text: The US ambrisentan label calls for a pregnancy test before starting and advises effective contraception before starting, during treatment and for one month after stopping.
before_after.quote: Obtain a pregnancy test prior to initiation of treatment with Letairis. Advise patients who can become pregnant to use effective contraception prior to initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for one month after discontinuation of treatment with Letairis.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Letairis (ambrisentan), Gilead Sciences, section 5.1 Embryo-fetal Toxicity, via openFDA

paternal.quote: Decreases in sperm count have been observed in patients taking ERAs. Macitentan, like other ERAs, may have an adverse effect on spermatogenesis in men.
paternal.source_label: EMA, Opsumit (macitentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 (Male fertility)

monitoring.text: EMA recommends monthly pregnancy tests while a woman of childbearing potential takes ambrisentan.
monitoring.quote: Monthly pregnancy tests during treatment with ambrisentan are recommended.
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Volibris (ambrisentan) Summary of Product Characteristics, section 4.6 Fertility, pregnancy and lactation

evidence_base.text: FDA's 2025 decision rested on human fetal outcomes reported from 2001 to 2024 after exposure to any ERA, which showed no pattern of malformations like those seen in animals.
evidence_base.quote: based on an evaluation of human fetal outcomes reported from 2001 to 2024 after exposure to a drug in the endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) pharmacologic class. These data have not shown a pattern of congenital malformations
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA, supplement approval letter NDA 022081/S-045 (Letairis), removal of the Ambrisentan REMS

regulatory.text: French product information contraindicates cyclophosphamide in pregnancy and in women of childbearing age who do not use effective contraception.
regulatory.quote: Par conséquent, le cyclophosphamide est contre-indiqué chez la femme enceinte et chez les femmes en âge de procréer n’utilisant pas de contraception efficace.
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, ENDOXAN 1000 mg RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

window.text: The US label reports malformations of the skeleton, palate, limbs and eyes, and miscarriage, after cyclophosphamide exposure in the first trimester.
window.quote: Malformations of the skeleton, palate, limbs and eyes as well as miscarriage have been reported after exposure to cyclophosphamide in the first trimester.
window.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.1 Human Data, via openFDA

dose.text: Animal data in the US label show cyclophosphamide given to pregnant mice, rats, rabbits and monkeys at doses at or below the human dose caused malformations, including limb and digit defects.
dose.quote: Administration of cyclophosphamide to pregnant mice, rats, rabbits and monkeys during the period of organogenesis at doses at or below the dose in patients based on body surface area resulted in various malformations
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.1 Animal Data, via openFDA

effects.text: French product information describes a fairly consistent malformation pattern including limb anomalies, eye defects, craniosynostosis, facial dysmorphism, hydrocephalus and microcephaly.
effects.quote: En clinique, des cas de malformations avec un tableau malformatif assez homogène (anomalies de membres, atteintes de l’œil, craniosténoses, dysmorphies faciales, atteintes du système nerveux central à type d’hydrocéphalie et microcéphalie)
effects.source_label: ANSM, ENDOXAN 1000 mg RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

other_effects.text: The US label reports fetal growth retardation and newborn toxicity, including leukopenia, anemia, pancytopenia, severe bone marrow hypoplasia and gastroenteritis, after cyclophosphamide exposure.
other_effects.quote: Fetal growth retardation and toxic effects manifesting in the newborn, including leukopenia, anemia, pancytopenia, severe bone marrow hypoplasia, and gastroenteritis have been reported after exposure to cyclophosphamide.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.1 Human Data, via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review found an apparent major malformation rate of 18% (7/40) after first-trimester cyclophosphamide exposure in published cases, against 3% in the US general population.
absolute_risk.quote: the apparent rate of major malformations following exposure to cyclophosphamide during the first trimester was 18% (7/40 conceptuses, based on 36 liveborn infants and examination of the fetuses of 2 stillbirths and 2 induced abortions)
absolute_risk.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.11 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

before_after.text: The US label asks prescribers to verify pregnancy status before starting and advises women to use effective contraception during treatment and for up to 1 year afterwards.
before_after.quote: Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with Cyclophosphamide for Injection and for up to 1 year after completion of therapy.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.3, via openFDA

paternal.text: The US label advises men with partners who could become pregnant to use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 months after it ends, based on genotoxicity and animal data.
paternal.quote: Based on findings in genetic toxicity and animal reproduction studies, advise male patients with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with Cyclophosphamide for Injection and for 4 months after completion of therapy
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.3, via openFDA

monitoring.text: If the pregnancy continues, French product information requires specialised prenatal screening targeted at cyclophosphamide malformations and neonatal monitoring, especially haematological and cardiac.
monitoring.quote: En cas de poursuite de la grossesse, un dépistage prénatal spécialisé, ciblé sur les malformations décrites avec le cyclophosphamide est nécessaire ; ainsi qu’une surveillance néonatale (en particulier hématologique et cardiaque).
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, ENDOXAN 1000 mg RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

evidence_base.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review documents 416 cyclophosphamide-exposed pregnancies from published reports in cancer patients, 413 cases given as polytherapy and only 6 as monotherapy.
evidence_base.quote: A total of 416 pregnancies and 419 conceptuses were exposed to cyclophosphamide on account of 3 sets of twins
evidence_base.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.11 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

regulatory.source_label: ANSM, ENDOXAN 1000 mg RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

window.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.1 Human Data, via openFDA

dose.quote: Administration of cyclophosphamide to pregnant mice, rats, rabbits and monkeys during the period of organogenesis at doses at or below the dose in patients based on body surface area resulted in various malformations
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.1 Animal Data, via openFDA

effects.source_label: ANSM, ENDOXAN 1000 mg RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

other_effects.quote: Fetal growth retardation and toxic effects manifesting in the newborn, including leukopenia, anemia, pancytopenia, severe bone marrow hypoplasia, and gastroenteritis have been reported after exposure to cyclophosphamide.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.1 Human Data, via openFDA

before_after.quote: Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with Cyclophosphamide for Injection and for up to 1 year after completion of therapy.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Cyclophosphamide for Injection (Baxter, ANDA040745), section 8.3, via openFDA
