evidence_base.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.11 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

regulatory.text: French product information for Efudix 5% cream contraindicates locally applied fluorouracil during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
regulatory.quote: L’utilisation de fluorouracile administré par voie locale est contre-indiquée pendant la grossesse et l’allaitement
regulatory.source_label: ANSM, EFUDIX 5% crème RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

window.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review found that major malformations followed first-trimester fluorouracil exposure, with an adjusted rate of 1% (2/161) after second- and/or third-trimester-only exposure.
window.quote: the adjusted apparent rate of major malformations following exposure to 5-fluorouracil in the second and/or third trimester only was 1% (2/161 conceptuses, based on 161 liveborn infants)
window.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

dose.text: In mice, intraperitoneal fluorouracil at 10 mg/kg or more, about 0.06 times a 12 mg/kg human dose by body surface area, caused cleft palate, skeletal defects and deformed paws and tails in animal studies.
dose.quote: Malformations including cleft palate, skeletal defects and deformed appendages (paws and tails) were observed when fluorouracil was administered by intraperitoneal injection to mice at doses at or above 10 mg/kg
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Fluorouracil Injection (Fresenius Kabi, ANDA040278), section 8.1/8.6 Animal Data, via openFDA

effects.text: A 2013 US NTP systematic review suggests a possible pattern of craniofacial and skeletal malformations after first-trimester fluorouracil exposure, usually absent or fused fingers or toes.
effects.quote: There may be a pattern of craniofacial and/or skeletal malformations, usually involving the absence or fusion of the digits of the hand and/or foot, following first-trimester exposure
effects.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

other_effects.text: In the final 2013 NTP systematic review, 129 infants exposed to fluorouracil before birth were followed for 6 weeks to 17 years, and growth and development were normal in all but 4.
other_effects.quote: Normal growth and development were reported for all but 4 children.
other_effects.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

absolute_risk.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review reports an apparent rate of major malformations likely attributable to first-trimester fluorouracil exposure of 31% (4/13) in published cases, against 3% in the US general population.
absolute_risk.quote: the apparent rate of major malformations likely attributable to exposure to 5-fluorouracil in the first trimester was 31% (4/13 conceptuses, based on 10 liveborn infants and examination of the fetuses of 2 induced abortions and 1 stillbirth)
absolute_risk.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.4 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

before_after.text: Health Canada recommends a pregnancy test before starting intravenous fluorouracil and effective contraception during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose.
before_after.quote: An effective method of contraception should be used during treatment and for 6 months after the last dose of 5-fluorouracil.
before_after.source_label: Health Canada product monograph, Fluorouracil Injection USP (Accord Healthcare), sections 2 and 7

paternal.text: The US label says fluorouracil may damage sperm and advises men with partners who could become pregnant to use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after stopping.
paternal.quote: Fluorouracil may damage spermatozoa. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and for 3 months following cessation of therapy with fluorouracil
paternal.source_label: US FDA label, Fluorouracil Injection (Fresenius Kabi, ANDA040278), section 8.6, via openFDA

monitoring.text: After accidental use of Efudix cream in pregnancy, French product information says to stop treatment and follow the pregnancy with targeted prenatal monitoring, without systematically advising termination.
monitoring.quote: En cas d’administration accidentelle pendant la grossesse, le traitement doit être interrompu.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, EFUDIX 5% crème RCP sections 4.3 and 4.6, Base de données publique des médicaments (page updated 29/09/2026)

evidence_base.text: The final 2013 NTP systematic review documents 178 fluorouracil-exposed pregnancies from published reports in cancer patients, 17 of them in the first trimester and 172 on polytherapy.
evidence_base.quote: In utero exposure to 5-fluorouracil was documented for 178 pregnancies, including 1 twin pregnancy (179 conceptuses)
evidence_base.source_label: US National Toxicology Program (NIEHS), NTP Monograph on Developmental Effects and Pregnancy Outcomes Associated with Cancer Chemotherapy Use During Pregnancy, section 5.2.5 (final monograph, supersedes the prepublication copy)

regulatory.text: The US label contraindicates azathioprine for rheumatoid arthritis in pregnant women and says use in pregnancy should be avoided whenever possible, after careful weighing of risk and benefit.
regulatory.quote: IMURAN should not be given during pregnancy without careful weighing of risk versus benefit. Whenever possible, use of IMURAN in pregnant patients should be avoided. This drug should not be used for treating rheumatoid arthritis in pregnant women.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Imuran (Sebela), Contraindications and Warnings (effective 2025-11-08), via openFDA

window.text: ANSM says a newborn whose mother took azathioprine at the end of pregnancy may have anaemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia and/or thrombocytopenia.
window.quote: Un nouveau-né de mère traitée par l'azathioprine en fin de grossesse peut présenter une anémie, une leucopénie, une lymphopénie et/ou une thrombopénie.
window.source_label: ANSM, Imurel 50 mg comprimé pelliculé, RCP section 4.6 (updated 21/11/2025)

dose.text: ANSM says these newborn blood-count abnormalities are dose-dependent and usually transient, and that lowering the maternal dose when possible is desirable to prevent them.
dose.quote: Ces anomalies sont dose-dépendantes et habituellement transitoires. Afin d'éviter l'apparition de ces effets, une diminution de la posologie maternelle, lorsque cela est possible, est souhaitable
dose.source_label: ANSM, Imurel 50 mg comprimé pelliculé, RCP section 4.6 (updated 21/11/2025)

effects.text: A Swedish register study found an association between azathioprine exposure in early pregnancy and ventricular or atrial septal defects (adjusted OR 3.18, 95% CI 1.45-6.04).
effects.quote: An association between early pregnancy AZA exposure and ventricular/atrial septal defects was found (adjusted OR: 3.18, 95% CI: 1.45-6.04).
effects.source_label: Cleary and Källén, Birth Defects Res A 2009, Swedish Medical Birth Register, 476 exposed women (abstract)

other_effects.text: Health Canada says azathioprine can harm the fetus, including intra-uterine growth retardation, premature birth and low birth weight, particularly when combined with corticosteroids.
other_effects.quote: IMURAN can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman, including intra-uterine growth retardation, premature birth and low birth weight, particularly in combination with corticosteroids.
other_effects.source_label: Health Canada, Imuran product monograph, section 7.1.1 Pregnancy (authorized 2026-09-09)

absolute_risk.text: In a French nationwide registry of mothers with IBD, major malformations occurred in 197.2 per 10,000 births exposed to thiopurines in the first trimester versus 175.2 per 10,000 unexposed births.
absolute_risk.quote: The overall prevalence of MCMs ranged from 175.2 per 10,000 among unexposed births to 197.2 per 10,000 among those exposed to thiopurine
absolute_risk.source_label: Meyer et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2025, EPI-MERES French nationwide registry of mothers with IBD (abstract)

before_after.text: The Jayempi (azathioprine) SmPC, authorised centrally in the EU, says male and female patients of reproductive age must use contraception during treatment and for at least six months after it ends.
before_after.quote: contraceptive measures must be taken by both male and female patients of reproductive age during azathioprine therapy for at least six months after the end of azathioprine therapy.
before_after.source_label: EMA, Jayempi (azathioprine) SmPC, section 4.4 (product information updated 23/04/2026)

paternal.text: A 2023 meta-analysis of men with IBD found paternal thiopurine use was not associated with early pregnancy loss, preterm birth or congenital malformations (OR 1.07).
paternal.quote: Thiopurine use was not associated with risk of EPL (OR, 1.31; I2 = 19%; P = .17), PB (OR, 1.05; I2 = 0%; P = .20), or CM (OR, 1.07; I2 = 7%; P = .34).
paternal.source_label: Gubatan et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2023, systematic review and meta-analysis of paternal IBD medications (abstract)

monitoring.text: ANSM says the exposed newborn should have a full blood count, and live attenuated vaccines should be deferred until after 6 months of age as a precaution.
monitoring.quote: Une numération formule sanguine sera réalisée chez le nouveau-né. Le risque d'immunodépression néonatale conduit, par mesure de prudence, à différer l'administration de vaccins atténués vivants après 6 mois de vie.
monitoring.source_label: ANSM, Imurel 50 mg comprimé pelliculé, RCP section 4.6 (updated 21/11/2025)

evidence_base.text: The largest study read, a French nationwide registry, compared 5,223 births exposed to thiopurines in the first trimester with 28,827 unexposed births to mothers with IBD.
evidence_base.quote: Among a total of 39,515 births (5223 exposed to thiopurines, 6528 to anti-TNF, and 28,827 unexposed)
evidence_base.source_label: Meyer et al., Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2025, EPI-MERES French nationwide registry of mothers with IBD (abstract)

regulatory.text: The US label contraindicates penicillamine in pregnancy, except for the treatment of Wilson's disease or certain patients with cystinuria.
regulatory.quote: Except for the treatment of Wilson's disease or certain patients with cystinuria, use of penicillamine during pregnancy is contraindicated
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Contraindications (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

dose.text: In animal studies, the US label says penicillamine was teratogenic in rats at doses six times higher than the highest recommended human dose.
dose.quote: Penicillamine has been shown to be teratogenic in rats when given in doses six times higher than the highest dose recommended for human use.
dose.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Warnings: Pregnancy (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

effects.text: The US label says congenital cutis laxa and associated birth defects have been reported in babies exposed during pregnancy, although normal outcomes have also been reported.
effects.quote: Although normal outcomes have been reported, characteristic congenital cutis laxa and associated birth defects have been reported in infants born of mothers who received therapy with penicillamine during pregnancy.
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Warnings: Pregnancy (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

other_effects.text: The UK label reports several cases of reversible cutis laxa in infants whose mothers with Wilson's disease took penicillamine throughout pregnancy.
other_effects.quote: There have been several cases of reversible cutis laxa in infants born to mothers taking penicillamine throughout pregnancy.
other_effects.source_label: MHRA, Distamine 250 mg film-coated tablets SmPC, section 4.6 (revised 14/07/2026)

absolute_risk.text: Summarising the 2018 Pfeiffenberger cohort, a 2022 systematic review reports malformations in 3.3% of babies of mothers on penicillamine; it gives no numeric comparison rate for that figure.
absolute_risk.quote: Fetal malformations were observed in 3.3% of babies from mothers on DPA, 2.7% on trientine (comparable with the general population) and none on zinc.
absolute_risk.source_label: Litwin et al., Biomedicines 2022, systematic review and meta-analysis of pregnancy in Wilson's disease (PMC9495510), citing Pfeiffenberger et al. 2018

before_after.text: ANSM says treatment for Wilson disease must not be stopped during pregnancy and that, outside such cases, effective contraception is recommended.
before_after.quote: Dans le cas de la maladie de Wilson, le traitement ne doit pas être arrêté pendant la grossesse. En dehors de ces cas, une contraception efficace est recommandée.
before_after.source_label: ANSM, Trolovol 300 mg comprimé pelliculé, RCP section 4.6 (updated 25/02/2026)

monitoring.text: The US label says women of childbearing potential on penicillamine should promptly report a missed period and be followed closely for early recognition of pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: Women on therapy with penicillamine who are of childbearing potential should be apprised of this risk, advised to report promptly any missed menstrual periods or other indications of possible pregnancy, and followed closely for early recognition of pregnancy.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, Cuprimine (Bausch Health), Warnings: Pregnancy (effective 2026-01-26), via openFDA

evidence_base.text: The 2022 systematic review rests on 13 retrospective studies and 36 case series or reports, covering 822 pregnancies in 449 women with Wilson disease, not all exposed to penicillamine.
evidence_base.quote: We found 49 publications, including 13 retrospective studies and 36 series and case reports on pregnancy outcomes in WD patients. In total, descriptions of 449 pregnant women with 822 pregnancies were retrieved.
evidence_base.source_label: Litwin et al., Biomedicines 2022, systematic review and meta-analysis of pregnancy in Wilson's disease (PMC9495510)

regulatory.text: Japan's PMDA label for trimethadione (Minoale Powder, revised March 2022) lists pregnant women and women who may be pregnant under its contraindications.
regulatory.quote: 2.2 妊婦又は妊娠している可能性のある女性［9.5参照］
regulatory.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Minoale Powder 66.7% (trimethadione), Nichi-Iko, revised March 2022 (1st edition), section 2 Contraindications

effects.text: Japan's label cites an epidemiological survey in which epileptic women treated with trimethadione alone or combined in pregnancy had significantly more malformed babies (including cleft lip, cleft palate, heart defects) than a non-medicated group.
effects.quote: 妊娠中に本剤を単独又は併用投与されたてんかん患者の中に、奇形を有する児（口唇裂、口蓋裂、心奇形等）を出産した例が非服薬群と比較して有意に多いとの疫学的調査報告がある。
effects.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Minoale Powder 66.7% (trimethadione), Nichi-Iko, revised March 2022, section 9.5 Pregnant women

other_effects.text: The US label says reports suggest maternal anticonvulsants, particularly barbiturates, are associated with a neonatal coagulation defect that may cause bleeding usually within 24 hours of birth, possibly also with Tridione.
other_effects.quote: REPORTS HAVE SUGGESTED THAT THE MATERNAL INGESTION OF ANTICONVULSANT DRUGS, PARTICULARLY BARBITURATES, IS ASSOCIATED WITH A NEONATAL COAGULATION DEFECT THAT MAY CAUSE BLEEDING DURING THE EARLY (USUALLY WITHIN 24 HOURS OF BIRTH) NEONATAL PERIOD.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Tridione (trimethadione) tablets, AbbVie, Warnings: Usage During Pregnancy and Lactation (openFDA set_id b9322f58-ffcc-4831-5381-93a535b49a09, effective 2018-11-02)

before_after.text: The US label says effective contraception should accompany Tridione use in women of childbearing potential, and it states no duration after stopping and no pregnancy testing.
before_after.quote: EFFECTIVE MEANS OF CONTRACEPTION SHOULD ACCOMPANY THE USE OF TRIDIONE IN SUCH PATIENTS.
before_after.source_label: US FDA label, Tridione (trimethadione) tablets, AbbVie, Warnings: Usage During Pregnancy and Lactation (openFDA, effective 2018-11-02)

monitoring.text: The US label reports a suggestion to give prophylactic vitamin K to the mother one month before and during delivery, and intravenously to the infant immediately after birth.
monitoring.quote: IT HAS BEEN SUGGESTED THAT PROPHYLACTIC VITAMIN K BE GIVEN TO THE MOTHER ONE MONTH PRIOR TO, AND DURING DELIVERY, AND TO THE INFANT, INTRAVENOUSLY, IMMEDIATELY AFTER BIRTH.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, Tridione (trimethadione) tablets, AbbVie, Warnings: Usage During Pregnancy and Lactation (openFDA, effective 2018-11-02)

evidence_base.text: A Japanese multi-institutional collaborative study of 902 pregnancies in women with epilepsy estimated that the 11.5% malformation rate among treated mothers' live births would have been 6.75% had trimethadione been avoided.
evidence_base.quote: it was estimated that the rate would have been 6.75% among the treated group if trimethadione-treatment had been avoided
evidence_base.source_label: Nakane Y. Congenital malformation among infants of epileptic mothers treated during pregnancy: report of a collaborative study group in Japan. Folia Psychiatr Neurol Jpn 1979;33(3):363-9, PMID 520954 (PubMed abstract via NCBI efetch)

evidence_base.text: The US trimethadione label says birth-defect data from reports in the clinical literature are more extensive for paramethadione, trimethadione, phenytoin and phenobarbital than for other anticonvulsants.
evidence_base.quote: DATA ARE MORE EXTENSIVE WITH RESPECT TO TRIMETHADIONE, PARAMETHADIONE, PHENYTOIN AND PHENOBARBITAL THAN WITH OTHER ANTICONVULSANT DRUGS.
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label, Tridione (trimethadione) tablets, AbbVie, Warnings: Usage During Pregnancy and Lactation (openFDA set_id b9322f58-ffcc-4831-5381-93a535b49a09, effective 2018-11-02) — the only regulator text found that names paramethadione; no paramethadione-specific product information exists

regulatory.text: The US HICON label contraindicates sodium iodide I-131 in pregnancy because it crosses the placenta and fetal exposure can lead to neonatal hypothyroidism.
regulatory.quote: HICON ® is contraindicated in pregnancy because sodium iodide I 131 crosses the placenta and fetal exposure can lead to neonatal hypothyroidism.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

window.text: The fetal thyroid begins to concentrate iodide during the 10th to 12th week of gestation; the label does not state whether weeks count from conception or the last period.
window.quote: Sodium iodide I 131 crosses the placenta and the fetal thyroid begins to concentrate iodide during the 10 th to 12 th week of gestation.
window.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

dose.text: In literature reports of maternal doses of 333 to 8,325 MBq (9 to 225 mCi) at 4 to 26 weeks gestational age, the most common adverse outcome was hypothyroidism in infants and children.
dose.quote: maternal exposures to sodium iodide I 131 at doses of 333 MBq to 8,325 MBq (9 mCi to 225 mCi) during 4 to 26 weeks gestational age, the most common adverse outcomes were hypothyroid infants and children
dose.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

effects.text: Published reports describe neonatal thyroid abnormalities after fetal exposure, including thyroid agenesis (absent thyroid) and hypothyroidism.
effects.quote: Data from the published literature describe reports of neonatal thyroid abnormalities after fetal exposure; including agenesis of the thyroid and hypothyroidism
effects.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

other_effects.text: Late diagnosis of neonatal hypothyroidism after in utero exposure can lead to severe sequelae such as cognitive impairment and delayed bone age.
other_effects.quote: Delay in diagnosis of neonatal hypothyroidism after exposure to sodium iodide I 131 in utero can result in severe sequelae such as cognitive impairment and delayed bone age.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: In a Korean cohort of treated thyroid-cancer patients, malformation rates were 13.3% when conception occurred 0 to 5 months after radioiodine, against 7.9%, 8.3% and 9.6% for later intervals.
absolute_risk.quote: congenital malformation rates of 13.3% for the interval of 0 to 5 months, 7.9% for 6 to 11 months, 8.3% for 12 to 23 months, and 9.6% for 24 months or more
absolute_risk.source_label: Kim HO et al., Pregnancy outcomes and radioactive iodine treatment after thyroidectomy among women with thyroid cancer, JAMA Intern Med 2020 (Korean nationwide cohort)

before_after.text: The French SmPC requires effective contraception in men and women until 6 months after treatment of benign disease and until 12 months after treatment of thyroid cancer.
before_after.quote: une contraception efficace sera mise en place et maintenue chez l'homme et la femme jusqu'à 6 mois après traitement d'une affection bénigne et jusqu'à 12 mois après traitement d'un cancer thyroïdien
before_after.source_label: ANSM, RCP Iodure (131 I) de sodium pour therapie Curiumpharma 37-7 400 MBq, gelule

paternal.text: The French SmPC advises men treated with radioiodine to wait 6 to 12 months before fathering a child, so that irradiated sperm are replaced.
paternal.quote: Il doit être recommandé aux hommes traités par l'iode radioactif d'attendre 6 à 12 mois avant de procréer, le temps que les spermatozoïdes irradiés soient remplacés par des non irradiés.
paternal.source_label: ANSM, RCP Iodure (131 I) de sodium pour therapie Curiumpharma 37-7 400 MBq, gelule

monitoring.text: The US label says to monitor thyroid function in any infant born after in utero exposure to sodium iodide I-131.
monitoring.quote: Monitor thyroid function in any infant born after in utero exposure to sodium iodide I 131.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label, HICON sodium iodide I 131 (Jubilant DraxImage), via openFDA

evidence_base.text: For conception after thyroid-cancer treatment, a meta-analysis of seven observational studies with 13,811 pregnancies found no significant effect on congenital malformation (OR 1.00).
evidence_base.quote: Seven observational studies were eligible, involving 125,591 participants and 13,811 pregnancies.
evidence_base.source_label: Zhang L et al., The effect of I-131 therapy on pregnancy outcomes after thyroidectomy in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: a meta-analysis, Endocrine 2021

regulatory.text: Propylthiouracil may be the treatment of choice when an antithyroid drug is indicated during or just prior to the first trimester of pregnancy, per the US boxed warning on liver injury.
regulatory.quote: Propylthiouracil may be the treatment of choice when an antithyroid drug is indicated during or just prior to the first trimester of pregnancy
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, propylthiouracil tablets (Macleods), via openFDA

window.text: The sensitive window for malformations is gestational week 6 to 10 counted from the last menstrual period, equivalent to embryonic week 4 to 8 from conception.
window.quote: During gestational week 6–10 (embryonic week 4–8), tissues and organs rapidly develop, and it is the period that is most sensitive to teratogenic exposures and abnormal development.
window.source_label: Andersen SL et al., Severity of birth defects after propylthiouracil exposure in early pregnancy, Thyroid 2014 (Danish nationwide registry cohort)

dose.text: A meta-analysis notes that the only study reporting a dose-response found larger malformation risks with high cumulative methimazole or carbimazole doses, but not with PTU.
dose.quote: This was also the only study to report a dose–response relationship and observed larger risk estimates for congenital anomalies with high cumulative doses of CBZ/MMI but not with PTU.
dose.source_label: Morales DR et al., Antithyroid drug use during pregnancy and the risk of birth defects: systematic review and meta-analysis, Br J Clin Pharmacol 2021

effects.text: Danish registry cases after early-pregnancy PTU were face and neck defects (preauricular and branchial sinus, fistula or cyst) and urinary defects (single kidney cyst, hydronephrosis).
effects.quote: 7 children were diagnosed with a birth defect in the face and neck region (preauricular and branchial sinus/fistula/cyst) and 7 children had a birth defect in the urinary system (single cyst of kidney and hydronephrosis)
effects.source_label: Andersen SL et al., Severity of birth defects after propylthiouracil exposure in early pregnancy, Thyroid 2014 (Danish nationwide registry cohort)

other_effects.text: PTU crosses the placenta and can cause fetal goiter and cretinism (congenital hypothyroidism) when given to a pregnant woman.
other_effects.quote: Propylthiouracil crosses the placenta and can cause fetal goiter and cretinism when administered to a pregnant woman
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, propylthiouracil tablets (Macleods), via openFDA

absolute_risk.text: In a Danish nationwide cohort, birth defects diagnosed before age 2 affected 8.3% of children exposed to PTU in early pregnancy, against 6.7% of nonexposed children.
absolute_risk.quote: The overall frequency of birth defects was 6.7% (95% CI, 6.7% to 6.8%) in nonexposed children and higher after exposure to methimazole/carbimazole (9.6%; 95% CI, 8.2% to 11.2%) and propylthiouracil (8.3%; 95% CI, 6.7% to 10.3%).
absolute_risk.source_label: Andersen SL et al., Maternal thyroid function, use of antithyroid drugs in early pregnancy, and birth defects, J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2019 (Danish nationwide cohort)

before_after.text: Health Canada suggests PTU before conception and in the first trimester where clinically appropriate, because methimazole carries a higher risk of congenital abnormalities during first-trimester organogenesis.
before_after.quote: is suggested for use prior to conception and in the first trimester of pregnancy where clinically appropriate due to the higher risk of congenital abnormalities with methimazole during fetal organogenesis in the first trimester
before_after.source_label: Health Canada product monograph, Propylthiouracil Tablets (Phebra Canada)

monitoring.text: In 2019 the EMA's PRAC asked that EU product information state that close maternal, foetal and neonatal monitoring is recommended whenever propylthiouracil is used during pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: If propylthiouracil is used during pregnancy, close maternal, foetal and neonatal monitoring is recommended.
monitoring.source_label: EMA PRAC recommendations on signals, propylthiouracil and risk of congenital anomalies (EPITT 19358), EMA/PRAC/303951/2019

evidence_base.text: A 2022 meta-analysis pooled 16 cohort studies including 15,785 PTU exposures and found an adjusted risk ratio of 1.16 for congenital anomalies against nondisease controls.
evidence_base.quote: We identified 16 cohort studies comprising 5957, 15,785, and 15,666 exposures to CMZ/MMI, PTU, and untreated hyperthyroidism, respectively.
evidence_base.source_label: Agrawal M et al., Antithyroid drug therapy in pregnancy and risk of congenital anomalies: systematic review and meta-analysis, Clin Endocrinol 2022

regulatory.text: Ireland's approved label contraindicates amiodarone during pregnancy, except in exceptional circumstances, because of its effect on the fetal thyroid gland.
regulatory.quote: In view of its effect on the foetal thyroid gland, amiodarone is contraindicated during pregnancy, except in exceptional circumstances.
regulatory.source_label: HPRA (Ireland) SmPC, Cordarone X 200mg Tablets, section 4.6

window.text: France's ANSM says the fetal thyroid starts taking up iodine from 14 weeks counted from the last menstrual period, so no fetal thyroid effect is expected from earlier administration.
window.quote: La thyroïde fœtale commençant à fixer l'iode à partir de 14 semaines d'aménorrhée, aucun retentissement sur la thyroïde fœtale n'est attendu en cas d'administrations préalables.
window.source_label: ANSM (France) RCP, Cordarone 200 mg comprimé sécable, section 4.6

dose.text: In animal studies, amiodarone given to rabbits, rats and mice during organogenesis caused embryo-fetal toxicity at doses below the maximum recommended human maintenance dose.
dose.quote: administration of amiodarone to rabbits, rats, and mice during organogenesis resulted in embryo-fetal toxicity at doses less than the maximum recommended human maintenance dose
dose.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), amiodarone hydrochloride tablets, section 8.1

effects.text: France's ANSM states that clinical data are not currently relevant enough to assess a possible malformation risk when amiodarone is given in the first trimester.
effects.quote: En clinique, il n'existe pas actuellement de données suffisamment pertinentes pour évaluer un éventuel effet malformatif de l'amiodarone lorsqu'elle est administrée au premier trimestre de la grossesse.
effects.source_label: ANSM (France) RCP, Cordarone 200 mg comprimé sécable, section 4.6

other_effects.text: The US label says amiodarone use in pregnancy may increase the risk of neonatal hypo- and hyperthyroidism, neonatal bradycardia, neurodevelopmental abnormalities, preterm birth and fetal growth restriction.
other_effects.quote: amiodarone use in pregnant women may increase the risk for fetal adverse effects including neonatal hypo- and hyperthyroidism, neonatal bradycardia, neurodevelopmental abnormalities, preterm birth and fetal growth restriction
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), amiodarone hydrochloride tablets, section 8.1

absolute_risk.text: In a 2026 meta-analysis of seven single-arm case series of fetuses given amiodarone-inclusive treatment for tachyarrhythmia, the pooled incidence of thyroid dysfunction was 21.2%, with no comparison group.
absolute_risk.quote: The pooled incidence of thyroid dysfunction was 21.2% (95% CI:11.4%–32.6%).
absolute_risk.source_label: Kong L et al., Front Pharmacol 2026;17:1912369, systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42024560291)

before_after.text: Ireland's label says that if stopping amiodarone before a planned conception is considered, given its long half-life, the real risk of recurrent life-threatening arrhythmia should be weighed against the unknown fetal hazard.
before_after.quote: because of the long half life of Cordarone X, discontinuation of the drug is considered prior to planned conception, the real risk of recurrence of life threatening arrhythmias should be weighed against the unknown possible hazard for the foetus
before_after.source_label: HPRA (Ireland) SmPC, Cordarone X 200mg Tablets, section 4.6

monitoring.text: The US label says to monitor the newborn for signs and symptoms of thyroid disorder and cardiac arrhythmias after amiodarone exposure in pregnancy.
monitoring.quote: Monitor the newborn for signs and symptoms of thyroid disorder and cardiac arrhythmias.
monitoring.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), amiodarone hydrochloride tablets, section 8.1

evidence_base.text: A 2026 systematic review of amiodarone for fetal tachyarrhythmia analysed 107 treated pregnancies from 27 studies, which included case reports and case series.
evidence_base.quote: We analyzed 107 pregnancies treated with amiodarone from 27 studies.
evidence_base.source_label: Kong L et al., Front Pharmacol 2026;17:1912369, systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42024560291)

regulatory.text: Japan's Tigason label opens with a warning that etretinate is teratogenic and must not be given to pregnant women or to women who may be pregnant.
regulatory.quote: 本剤には催夺形性があるので、姊婦又は姊娠している可能性のある女性には投与しないこと。
regulatory.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Tigason capsules 10/25 (etretinate), section 1 Warning

effects.text: The US acitretin label lists fetal abnormalities reported with acitretin and/or etretinate, including meningomyelocele, facial dysmorphia, syndactyly, absent terminal phalanges and malformations of hip, ankle and forearm.
effects.quote: Major human fetal abnormalities associated with acitretin and/or etretinate administration have been reported including meningomyelocele; meningoencephalocele; multiple synostoses; facial dysmorphia; syndactyly; absence of terminal phalanges; malformations of hip, ankle, and forearm
effects.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), acitretin capsules, boxed Contraindications and Warnings

other_effects.text: For conceptions after the last etretinate or acitretin dose, the US label lists reported abnormal outcomes including premature birth, neonatal apnoea or anaemia, hypotonia and hypocalcaemia, without judging retinoid causation.
other_effects.quote: 15 of the outcomes were abnormal (including cases of absent hand/wrist, clubfoot, GI malformation, hypocalcemia, hypotonia, limb malformation, neonatal apnea/anemia, neonatal ichthyosis, placental disorder/death, undescended testicle, and 5 cases of premature birth)
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), acitretin capsules, boxed Contraindications and Warnings

before_after.text: Japan's label says a woman who could become pregnant and must take etretinate has to use contraception during treatment and for at least 2 years after stopping.
before_after.quote: 姊娠する可能性のある女性で他に代わるべき治療法がない重症な患者にやむを得ず投与する場合には、投与中及び投与中止後少なくとも２年間は避姊させること。
before_after.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Tigason capsules 10/25 (etretinate), section 8.2.2

paternal.text: Japan's label, citing animal (guinea pig) reports of abnormal sperm formation, tells men taking etretinate to use contraception during treatment and for at least 6 months after stopping.
paternal.quote: 本剤はモルモットを用いた動物実験で、精子形成能に異常を起こすことが報告されているので男性に投与する場合には、投与中及び投与中止後少なくとも６ヶ月間は避姊させること。
paternal.source_label: PMDA (Japan) package insert, Tigason capsules 10/25 (etretinate), section 8.2.3

evidence_base.text: The US acitretin label counts 318 prospectively reported pregnancies exposed to etretinate, acitretin or both, with conception after the last etretinate dose in 103 of them.
evidence_base.quote: There have been 318 prospectively reported cases involving pregnancies and the use of etretinate, acitretin or both. In 238 of these cases, the conception occurred after the last dose of etretinate (103 cases), acitretin (126), or both (9).
evidence_base.source_label: US FDA label (openFDA), acitretin capsules, boxed Contraindications and Warnings

regulatory.text: Austria's Marcoumar label contraindicates phenprocoumon in pregnancy, with one exception: an absolute need for anticoagulation when heparin intolerance is life-threatening.
regulatory.quote: Schwangerschaft; Ausnahme: absolute Indikation zur Antikoagulation bei lebensbedrohlicher Heparin-Unverträglichkeit (siehe Abschnitt 4.6).
regulatory.source_label: Austrian BASG Fachinformation (SmPC), Marcoumar Tabletten (phenprocoumon 3 mg), Z.Nr. 8096, Stand der Information 06.2026, section 4.3 Gegenanzeigen

window.text: The Swiss label states that the rate of serious birth defects is strongly raised when phenprocoumon treatment continues beyond the fifth week of gestation.
window.quote: le taux de malformations congénitales graves est fortement élevé lorsque le traitement par phenprocoumone est poursuivi au-delà de la cinquième semaine de gestation
window.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

dose.text: A systematic review of women with mechanical heart valves cites registry data that did not show less fetal loss with low first-trimester VKA doses, defined for phenprocoumon as 3 mg per day or less.
dose.quote: recent data from the Registry of Pregnancy and Cardiac disease (ROPAC) registry did not demonstrate reduced foetal loss with the use of low first-trimester doses of VKAs [warfarin ≤5 mg/day, acenocoumarol ≤2 mg/day or phenprocoumon ≤3 mg/day)]
dose.source_label: D'Souza R et al. Anticoagulation for pregnant women with mechanical heart valves: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur Heart J 2017;38(19):1509-1516 (PMC5429939), Discussion

effects.text: Citing warfarin, the Swiss label reports chondrodysplasia (Conradi-Hünermann) after first-trimester exposure and growth disorders with microcephaly and optic atrophy after second- and third-trimester exposure.
effects.quote: Lors d'exposition à la warfarine, des chondrodysplasies (maladie de Conradi-Hünermann) ont été observées au cours du 1er trimestre de gestation, ainsi que des troubles de la croissance avec microencéphalie et atrophie du nerf optique aux 2e et 3e trimestres.
effects.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Données précliniques, Toxicité sur la reproduction

other_effects.text: The Swiss label warns that exposure in the second and third trimesters raises the fetal risk of intrauterine or birth-related (cerebral) bleeding from fetal anticoagulation.
other_effects.quote: Dans les cas d'exposition au phenprocoumone au cours des deuxième et troisième trimestres de grossesse, il existe, pour le fœtus, un risque accru d'hémorragie (cérébrale) intra-utérine ou parturitionnelle résultant de l'anticoagulation fœtale.
other_effects.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

absolute_risk.text: In a cohort of 408 first-trimester phenprocoumon pregnancies, major birth defects occurred in 7.4% versus 2.3% of comparison pregnancies not exposed to VKA or other major teratogens (adjusted odds ratio 2.14).
absolute_risk.quote: the overall rate of major birth defects was significantly increased (7.4 % vs 2.3 %; adjusted odds ratio [ORadj] 2.14; 95 % confidence interval [CI] 1.4-3.4)
absolute_risk.source_label: Hüttel E et al. Pregnancy outcome of first trimester exposure to the vitamin K antagonist phenprocoumon depends on duration of treatment. Thromb Haemost 2017;117(5):870-879 (PMID 28229160), abstract

before_after.text: The Swiss label states that women of childbearing age taking phenprocoumon must use effective contraception during treatment and for three months after the last dose.
before_after.quote: Les femmes en âge de procréer qui prennent Marcoumar doivent utiliser des mesures contraceptives efficaces au cours du traitement et pendant les trois mois suivant la dernière dose.
before_after.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs on phenprocoumon, the Swiss label advises an immediate switch to a safer treatment such as heparin and close pregnancy follow-up including level II ultrasound.
monitoring.quote: Si une grossesse survient chez une patiente prenant Marcoumar, il convient d'instaurer immédiatement un traitement alternatif plus sûr (p.ex. héparine) et de suivre la grossesse de près, y compris au moyen d'échographies de niveau II.
monitoring.source_label: Swissmedic-approved professional information (AIPS), Marcoumar 3 mg comprimés (phenprocoumon), Viatris Pharma GmbH, authorisation 19395, updated October 2020, section Grossesse, allaitement

evidence_base.text: The largest phenprocoumon-specific study read is an observational cohort comparing 408 exposed pregnancies with 1,642 pregnancies unexposed to VKA or other major teratogens.
evidence_base.quote: Four hundred eight pregnancies with phenprocoumon exposure were compared to 1,642 pregnancies neither exposed to VKA nor to other major teratogens or fetotoxicants.
evidence_base.source_label: Hüttel E et al. Pregnancy outcome of first trimester exposure to the vitamin K antagonist phenprocoumon depends on duration of treatment. Thromb Haemost 2017;117(5):870-879 (PMID 28229160), abstract

window.text: The US label states that methotrexate exposure in the first trimester, counted by trimester of pregnancy, is associated with more miscarriages and multiple developmental problems.
window.quote: Methotrexate exposure during the first trimester of pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of spontaneous abortions and multiple adverse developmental outcomes
window.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, section 8.1 Pregnancy (read via openFDA)

dose.text: The EMA says data are insufficient for exposure in pregnancy above 30 mg a week, but higher rates of miscarriage and malformations are expected, particularly at doses used to treat cancer.
dose.quote: Insufficient data is available for methotrexate exposure during pregnancy higher than 30 mg (15 ml)/week, but higher rates of spontaneous abortions and congenital malformations are expected, in particular at doses commonly used in oncologic indications
dose.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6

effects.text: First-trimester exposure is associated with skull, facial, central nervous system and limb abnormalities (limb defects flagged), and sometimes heart defects and intellectual impairment.
effects.quote: multiple adverse developmental outcomes, including skull anomalies, facial dysmorphism, central nervous system abnormalities, limb abnormalities, and sometimes cardiac anomalies and intellectual impairment
effects.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, section 8.1 Pregnancy (read via openFDA)

absolute_risk.text: Major birth defects occurred in 6.6% of babies born alive after low-dose methotrexate in pregnancy, compared with about 4% of babies born alive to women with the same diseases on other medicines.
absolute_risk.quote: Major birth defects occurred in 6.6% of live births in women exposed to low-dose methotrexate treatment (less than 30 mg [15 ml]/week) during pregnancy, compared to approximately 4% of live births in disease-matched patients
absolute_risk.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6

before_after.text: The EU product information requires pregnancy to be excluded before use in non-cancer indications, and effective contraception in women of childbearing potential during treatment and for at least six months after.
before_after.quote: In non-oncologic indications, the absence of pregnancy must be confirmed before Jylamvo is used. If women of child bearing potential are treated, effective contraception must be used during treatment and for at least six months after.
before_after.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.4 (Teratogenicity – Reproductive risk)

paternal.text: As a precaution, the EU product information recommends reliable contraception for sexually active treated men or their female partners until at least 3 months after stopping, and no semen donation until 3 months after.
paternal.quote: recommended to use reliable contraception during treatment of the male patient and for at least 3 months after cessation of methotrexate. Men should not donate semen during therapy or for 3 months following discontinuation of methotrexate.
paternal.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6 (Contraception in males)

other_effects.text: The US label states that exposure in the second and third trimesters is associated with intrauterine growth restriction and functional abnormalities.
other_effects.quote: Adverse outcomes associated with exposure during second and third trimesters of pregnancy include intrauterine growth restriction and functional abnormalities.
other_effects.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, section 8.1 Pregnancy (read via openFDA)

regulatory.text: The US label carries a boxed warning that methotrexate tablets can cause embryo-fetal toxicity, including fetal death, and contraindicates them in pregnancy for non-cancer diseases.
regulatory.quote: WARNING: EMBRYO-FETAL TOXICITY, HYPERSENSITIVITY REACTIONS, SEVERE ADVERSE REACTIONS, AND RISK OF MEDICATION ERRORS Methotrexate tablets can cause embryo-fetal toxicity, including fetal death. For non-neoplastic diseases, methotrexate tablets are contraindicated in pregnancy.
regulatory.source_label: US FDA label, Trexall (methotrexate) tablets, Boxed Warning (read via openFDA)

monitoring.text: If pregnancy occurs during treatment or up to six months after, the EU product information says to give medical advice on the risk to the child and to perform ultrasound examinations.
monitoring.quote: If pregnancy occurs during treatment with methotrexate and up to six months thereafter, medical advice should be given regarding the risk of harmful effects on the child associated with treatment and ultrasonography examinations should be performed
monitoring.source_label: EMA, Jylamvo (methotrexate) EPAR product information, SmPC section 4.6 (Pregnancy)

evidence_base.text: A prospective multicentre cohort study included 324 pregnancies exposed to methotrexate at 30 mg/week or less, 188 after conception and 136 in the 12 weeks before, plus 459 disease-matched and 1,107 non-autoimmune comparison women.
evidence_base.quote: The study sample included 324 MTX-exposed pregnancies (188 exposed post-conception, 136 exposed pre-conception), 459 disease-matched comparison women, and 1,107 comparison women without autoimmune diseases.
evidence_base.source_label: Weber-Schoendorfer C et al., Arthritis Rheumatol 2014;66(5):1101-10, prospective multicenter cohort (PubMed abstract)

limit.text: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex III caps Retinol, Retinyl Acetate and Retinyl Palmitate at 0.05% Retinol Equivalent in body lotion and 0.3% RE in other leave-on and rinse-off products, under Regulation (EU) 2024/996.
limit.quote: For any cosmetic product containing Retinol, Retinyl Acetate or Retinyl Palmitate the following, labelling is obligatory: 'Contains Vitamin A. Consider your daily intake before use'.
limit.source_label: CosIng — EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III, entry 376 (European Commission, DG GROW)

effects.text: SCCS cites a prospective study in which mothers taking over 4500 mg retinol equivalent daily had a 3.5-fold higher risk of a child born with cranial-neural-crest defects.
effects.quote: Women taking more than 4500 mg RE of total Vitamin A (from food and supplement) daily had a 3.5 times higher risk of giving birth to a child with cranial-neural-crest defects
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1576/16 on Vitamin A (Retinol, Retinyl Acetate, Retinyl Palmitate), final version

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes vitamin A in cosmetics is safe at 0.05% RE in body lotion and 0.3% RE in other leave-on and rinse-off products; no numeric margin of safety is stated because the assessment compares exposure to a human tolerable upper intake level rather than an animal-study margin.
conclusion.quote: The SCCS is of the opinion that vitamin A in cosmetics at the concentrations of 0.05% Retinol Equivalent (RE) in body lotion, and 0.3% RE for other leave-on and rinse-off products is safe.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1639/21, revision of SCCS/1576/16 on Vitamin A, final version

limit.text: Annex III caps salicylic acid at 3.0% in rinse-off hair products, 2.0% in other leave-on products and 0.5% in body lotion, eye and lip products (Regulation (EU) 2021/850); Annex V separately allows 0.5% as a preservative (Regulation (EU) 2019/1966), both banned for children under 3.
limit.quote: Not to be used in preparations for children under 3 years of age. Not to be used in applications that may lead to exposure of the end-user's lungs by inhalation.
limit.source_label: CosIng — EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III entry 98 and Annex V entry 3 (European Commission, DG GROW)

basis_dose.text: SCCS bases its margin-of-safety calculation on a developmental NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day for teratogenicity in Wistar rats, from Tanaka et al. 1973a.
basis_dose.quote: The POD is expressed as a no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) of 75 mg/kg/day relating to the most sensitive toxic endpoint i.e. teratogenicity in the rat as the most sensitive species.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1601/18 on salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7), final opinion with corrigendum

effects.text: SCCS states salicylic acid's Repr. 2 (H361d) classification rests on developmental toxicity in both rats and monkeys, with teratogenic potency strong in rats and lower in monkeys.
effects.quote: salicylic acid was shown to have teratogenic properties but with species differences in potency: strong in rats and lower in monkeys
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1601/18 on salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7), final opinion with corrigendum

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes salicylic acid is safe as a 0.5% preservative and up to 3.0%/2.0% for other uses, citing a probabilistic margin of safety of 195 against the 75 mg/kg bw/day NOAEL.
conclusion.quote: The derived MOS with this scenario is 195 and thus demonstrates the safety of salicylic acid for cosmetics, excluding oral products such as toothpaste and mouthwash.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1601/18 on salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7), final opinion with corrigendum

limit.text: Annex III sets methyl salicylate limits ranging from 0.002% in eye makeup to 2.52% in toothpaste depending on product type, under Regulation (EU) 2023/1545, banned for children under 6 except in toothpaste.
limit.quote: Not to be used in preparations for children under 6 years of age, with the exception of (k) "Toothpaste".
limit.source_label: CosIng — EU Cosmetics Regulation 1223/2009, Annex III, entry 324 (European Commission, DG GROW)

basis_dose.text: SCCS bases its margin-of-safety calculation for methyl salicylate on a developmental NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day from a three-generation rat study by Collins, 1971.
basis_dose.quote: To assess the risk of MeS by systemic exposure, the SCCS has used the NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/d derived from the 3-generation study in rats by oral route (Collins et al., 1971).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1633/21 on methyl salicylate (methyl 2-hydroxybenzoate), final opinion

effects.text: At 150 mg/kg bw/day, methyl salicylate significantly decreased litter size, pup viability, survival and weaning data in the second generation of a three-generation rat study, and decreased pup body weight.
effects.quote: statistically significant decrease of litter size, viability (D0), survival (D4), weaning data in the second generation and decreased pup body weight at 150 mg/kg bw/day
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1633/21 on methyl salicylate (methyl 2-hydroxybenzoate), final opinion

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes methyl salicylate is safe at the dossier's maximum concentrations, with systemic margins of safety above 100 for adults and a lowest aggregate value of 108 for children aged 6-10.
conclusion.quote: For children, considering all products taken individually and also the aggregated exposure, the margin of safety is above 100.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion SCCS/1633/21 on methyl salicylate (methyl 2-hydroxybenzoate), final opinion

limit.text: EU Annex III entry 380 caps Hexyl Salicylate at 2% in hydroalcoholic fragrances, 0.5% in rinse-off products, 0.3% in leave-on products, 0.001% in toothpaste/mouthwash, and allows 0.1% in listed products made for children under 3.
limit.quote: Not to be used in preparations for children under 3 years of age, with the exception of (d) “Toothpaste” and (f).
limit.source_label: European Commission CosIng database, Annex III export (entry 380)

basis_dose.text: SCCS used a rat developmental NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day for salicylic acid, Hexyl Salicylate's hydrolysis product, as a read-across point of departure.
basis_dose.quote: SCCS uses the developmental NOAEL of 0.1% (75 mg/kg bw/day) derived from Tanaka et al. (1973a).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Hexyl Salicylate (SCCS/1658/23), final version of 28 February 2024

effects.text: SCCS bases Hexyl Salicylate's margin-of-safety calculation on teratogenic effects seen in orally dosed rats in the Tanaka 1973 study of its metabolite salicylic acid.
effects.quote: based upon the most sensitive observations in orally dosed rats, of teratogenic effects, in the Tanaka et al. 1973 study
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Hexyl Salicylate (SCCS/1658/23), final version of 28 February 2024

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes Hexyl Salicylate is safe at the Annex III concentrations, citing a systemic margin of safety above 100 despite concerns over potential endocrine-disrupting properties.
conclusion.quote: the SCCS considers Hexyl Salicylate safe when used up to the maximum concentrations as provided in Table 1 of this Opinion.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Hexyl Salicylate (SCCS/1658/23), final version of 28 February 2024

limit.text: EU Annex III entry 185 restricts Toluene to nail products at up to 25%, requiring warnings to keep it from children and limit use to adults.
limit.quote: Keep out of reach of children. To be used by adults only
limit.source_label: European Commission CosIng database, Annex III export (entry 185)

basis_dose.text: CIR selected a rat developmental NOAEL of 500 ppm (1875 mg/m3), converted to about 540 mg/kg bw/day orally, after applying a threefold uncertainty factor to a 1500 ppm LOAEL.
basis_dose.quote: 500 ppm (1875 mg/m3) was selected as the NOAEL for the DART endpoint.
basis_dose.source_label: CIR Final Amended Safety Assessment of Toluene as Used in Cosmetics

effects.text: In the pivotal rat gestational-exposure study, Toluene decreased maternal weight gain and fetal body weight at the 1500 ppm dose that set the LOAEL.
effects.quote: maternal weight gain of the test animals and fetal body weights in the 1500 ppm group were decreased
effects.source_label: CIR Final Amended Safety Assessment of Toluene as Used in Cosmetics

conclusion.text: CIR's Expert Panel concludes Toluene is safe in nail products up to 20%, below the EU's 25% Annex III limit, with DART margins of safety of at least 153.
conclusion.quote: The Expert Panel for Cosmetic Ingredient Safety concluded that Toluene is safe for use in nail products at concentrations up to 20%.
conclusion.source_label: CIR Final Amended Safety Assessment of Toluene as Used in Cosmetics

limit.text: EU Annex III entry 11 caps Dichlorophene at 0.5% in any cosmetic product and requires the label to state its presence.
limit.quote: Contains Dichlorophen
limit.source_label: European Commission CosIng database, Annex III export (entry 11)

conclusion.text: CIR's Expert Panel found the data insufficient to support Dichlorophene's safety, stating no reproductive or developmental toxicity data existed for the substance itself.
conclusion.quote: The CIR Expert Panel concludes that the available data are insufficient to support safety of Dichlorophene or Chlorophene.
conclusion.source_label: CIR Quick Reference Table (cir-safety.org), Dichlorophene entry, citing Yamarik, Int J Toxicol 23(Suppl. 1):1-27 (2004)

limit.text: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902 adds zinc pyrithione, Annex II entry 1670 (CAS 13463-41-7), to the list of substances banned in all cosmetic products, applying from 1 March 2022.
limit.quote: It should also be added to the list of substances prohibited in cosmetic products in Annex II to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009.
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902, recital 8 and Annex (EUR-Lex, read this session)

basis_dose.text: The SCCS derives a NOAEL of 0.75 mg/kg bw/day for maternal and developmental toxicity in rats dosed orally on gestation days 6 to 15.
basis_dose.quote: A NOAEL of 0.75 mg/kg/d is derived from the study for maternal and developmental toxicity.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Zinc Pyrithione, SCCS/1512/13 (revision of 18 June 2014)

effects.text: The SCCS reports skeletal and developmental malformations in most high-dose rat litters but states the substance is not a developmental toxicant since fetal effects occurred only alongside maternal toxicity.
effects.quote: However, as fetal effects occur at dosages where maternal toxicity is observed, the test article is not considered as a developmental toxicant.
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Zinc Pyrithione, SCCS/1512/13 (revision of 18 June 2014)

conclusion.text: The regulation that bans zinc pyrithione states the SCCS concluded in March 2020 it is safe up to 1% as a rinse-off anti-dandruff ingredient, the finding behind the EU's ban decision.
conclusion.quote: The SCCS concluded in its opinion of 3-4 March 2020 that Zinc Pyrithione can be considered safe when used as an anti-dandruff ingredient in rinse-off hair products up to a maximum concentration of 1 %.
conclusion.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902, recital 8 (EUR-Lex, read this session)

limit.text: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902 adds Butylphenyl Methylpropional, Annex II entry 1666 (CAS 80-54-6), to the cosmetics ban list, applying from 1 March 2022.
limit.quote: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union. It shall apply from 1 March 2022.
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1902 (EUR-Lex, read this session)

basis_dose.text: The SCCS sets the NOAEL for developmental toxicity at 4.5 mg/kg bw/day in an extended one-generation reproductive toxicity rat study, revising its earlier 5 mg/kg bw/day figure.
basis_dose.quote: The NOAEL for developmental toxicity in the F1 and F2 progeny was 3 mg/kg bw/d (equivalent to a mean overall oral dose of 4.5 mg/kg bw/d)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional (p-BMHCA), SCCS/1591/17, Final version

effects.text: The SCCS attributes lower F1 and F2 rat pup body weights, seen at the top dose, to maternal toxicity rather than a specific developmental effect.
effects.quote: based on reduced pup body weights in the F1 and F2 offspring, which were observed at 10 mg/kg bw/d
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional (p-BMHCA), SCCS/1591/17, Final version

conclusion.text: The SCCS concludes Lilial cannot be considered safe at the proposed fragrance concentrations once aggregate exposure from all product types is summed, giving a margin of safety of about 80 against the 4.5 mg/kg bw/day NOAEL.
conclusion.quote: However, considering the first-tier deterministic aggregate exposure, arising from the use of different product types together, Butylphenyl methylpropional at the proposed concentrations cannot be considered as safe.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Butylphenyl methylpropional (p-BMHCA), SCCS/1591/17, Final version

limit.text: The CosIng Annex II export lists TPO as entry 1731 (CAS 75980-60-8), banned in all cosmetic products under Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/877, replacing its former 5% Annex III nail-product entry.
limit.quote: 1731,"diphenyl(2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphine oxide; INCI: Trimethylbenzoyl Diphenylphosphine Oxide",75980-60-8,278-355-8,"(EU) 2025/877",,,,"TRIMETHYLBENZOYL DIPHENYLPHOSPHINE OXIDE",,18/06/2025
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex II export (European Commission, api.tech.ec.europa.eu)

basis_dose.text: The SCCS states no reproductive-toxicity data exist for TPO and instead bases its margin of safety on a 100 mg/kg bw/day NOAEL from 90-day rat studies showing testicular atrophy.
basis_dose.quote: an overall NOAEL of 100 mg/kg bw/day for repeated dose oral toxicity will be used for the calculation of the Margin of Safety (MoS)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide (TPO), SCCS/1528/14

conclusion.text: In 2014 the SCCS judged TPO safe as a nail-modelling product up to 5.0%, with a margin of safety of 1515 on the testicular-atrophy NOAEL, but the EU has since banned it outright after a CMR 1B reclassification.
conclusion.quote: The SCCS is of the opinion that Trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide (TPO) is safe when used as a nail modelling product at a concentration of at maximum 5.0%.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide (TPO), SCCS/1528/14

limit.text: NMP is banned from cosmetic products in the EU as Annex II entry 1393 under Regulation (EU) 2019/831, with a date of inclusion of 30 July 2020.
limit.quote: 1393,"N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone; 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidone",872-50-4,212-828-1,"(EU) 2019/831"
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex II export (European Commission, DG GROW), Last update 29/09/2026

basis_dose.text: The SCCS used the lowest oral developmental-toxicity NOAEL of 125 mg/kg bw/day in rats as the basis for its margin-of-safety calculation.
basis_dose.quote: The lowest NOAEL after oral administration of NMP in rats (125 mg/kg bw/day) is considered the most relevant observation and will be used in the calculation of MOS.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), SCCS/1413/11

effects.text: SCCS found embryolethal, teratogenic and fetotoxic developmental effects in rats, rabbits and mice after oral, dermal or intraperitoneal NMP exposure.
effects.quote: The developmental effects in animals consisted in embryolethal, teratogenic, and fetotoxic effects after oral (gavage) and dermal administration in rats, after oral (gavage) treatment in rabbits, and i.p. injection of mice.
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), SCCS/1413/11

conclusion.text: SCCS calculated a margin of safety of 8.4 for NMP at a worst-case 5% use concentration and concluded that this is not safe for the consumer.
conclusion.quote: the SCCS is of the opinion that the presence of NMP with a maximum use concentration of 5% in cosmetic products is not safe for the consumer.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), SCCS/1413/11

limit.text: Theophylline is banned from cosmetic products in the EU as Annex II entry 1710 under Regulation (EU) 2023/1490, with a date of inclusion of 24 August 2023.
limit.quote: 1710,"Theophylline; 1,3-dimethyl-3,7-dihydro-1H-purine-2,6-dione",58-55-9,200-385-7,"(EU) 2023/1490"
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex II export (European Commission, DG GROW), Last update 29/09/2026

basis_dose.text: CIR reports a reproductive-toxicity NOAEL of 75 mg/kg bw/day and a LOAEL of 150 mg/kg bw/day for decreased testicular weight in rats, not a developmental-toxicity dose.
basis_dose.quote: A significant decrease in testicular weight was apparent in rats with 150 mg/kg bw/d by gavage, but not in rats given 75 mg/kg bw or less.
basis_dose.source_label: CIR Safety Assessment of Methylxanthines, Final Report

effects.text: CIR reports that theophylline in drinking water during gestation reduced litter size and fetal weight in rats without increasing malformations.
effects.quote: A reduction of litter size and fetal weight was noted, but no increases in malformations.
effects.source_label: CIR Safety Assessment of Methylxanthines, Final Report

conclusion.text: CIR's expert panel concluded that caffeine, theobromine and theophylline are safe in cosmetics at their present practices of use and concentration, without calculating a margin of safety.
conclusion.quote: The CIR Expert Panel concluded that Caffeine, Theobromine, and Theophylline are safe in cosmetics in the present practices of use and concentration described in this safety assessment.
conclusion.source_label: CIR Safety Assessment of Methylxanthines, Final Report

limit.text: Boric acid and other borates have been banned in the EU since 29/30 July 2020 under Regulations (EU) 2019/831 and (EU) 2019/1966, and sodium perborate was re-listed under Regulation (EU) 2026/78 from 15 January 2026.
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex II export (European Commission, DG GROW), Last update 29/09/2026

basis_dose.text: SCCS used a developmental-toxicity NOAEL of 55 mg boric acid/kg bw/day (9.6 mg boron/kg bw/day) across rat, mouse and rabbit studies.
basis_dose.quote: A NOAEL for pre-natal effects in all 3 species has been established at 55 mg/kg bw/day (9.6 mg B/kg bw/day).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

effects.text: SCCS reports that boric acid exposure during pregnancy caused decreased fetal body weight and cardiovascular and rib malformations in rats, mice and rabbits.
effects.quote: Exposure to boric acid during pregnancy (given either throughout gestation or only during major organogenesis) resulted in decreased foetal body weight, and foetal cardiovascular and rib malformations in the rat, mouse and rabbit.
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

conclusion.text: SCCS concluded in 2010 that boric acid, borates and tetraborates were safe within Annex III concentration limits, with a margin of safety of 480, before the EU later banned them outright.
conclusion.quote: boric acid, borates and tetraborates are safe when used under the conditions laid down in entry 1a of Annex III.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

boric acid [1].documented_as: boric acid and the borates as a group
