basis_dose.text: SCCS used a developmental-toxicity NOAEL of 55 mg boric acid/kg bw/day (9.6 mg boron/kg bw/day) across rat, mouse and rabbit studies.
basis_dose.quote: A NOAEL for pre-natal effects in all 3 species has been established at 55 mg/kg bw/day (9.6 mg B/kg bw/day).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

effects.text: SCCS reports that boric acid exposure during pregnancy caused decreased fetal body weight and cardiovascular and rib malformations in rats, mice and rabbits.
effects.quote: Exposure to boric acid during pregnancy (given either throughout gestation or only during major organogenesis) resulted in decreased foetal body weight, and foetal cardiovascular and rib malformations in the rat, mouse and rabbit.
effects.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

conclusion.text: SCCS concluded in 2010 that boric acid, borates and tetraborates were safe within Annex III concentration limits, with a margin of safety of 480, before the EU later banned them outright.
conclusion.quote: boric acid, borates and tetraborates are safe when used under the conditions laid down in entry 1a of Annex III.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS Opinion on Boron Compounds, SCCS/1249/09

tetraboron disodium heptaoxide, hydrate.documented_as: boric acid and the borates as a group

limit.text: EU law bans Quaternium-15's CMR cis-isomer in cosmetics under Annex II (entries 1385-1386) since Regulation (EU) 2019/831 of 22 May 2019, which deleted its prior 0.2% Annex V preservative allowance.
limit.quote: Quaternium-15 should be deleted from the list of preservatives allowed in cosmetic products in Annex V to Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 and added to the list of substances prohibited in cosmetic products in Annex II
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/831 of 22 May 2019, recital 6 and Annex entries 1385-1386 (OJ L 137/29-30, 23.5.2019)

basis_dose.text: In Fischer 344 rats dosed by gavage in 1981, the sponsor proposed a NOEL of 5 mg/kg bw/day for maternal and foetal toxicity, which SCCS says should rather be considered a LOAEL.
basis_dose.quote: The applicant deduced a NOEL of 5 mg/kg bw/day for maternal and foetal toxicity.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS/1344/10, Opinion on Quaternium-15 (cis-isomer), section 3.3.8.2

effects.text: In Fischer 344 rats, cis-CTAC caused fetal eye malformations, mainly microphthalmia and anophthalmia, most frequent at 25 and 75 mg/kg bw/day gavage doses.
effects.quote: The majority of the malformed foetuses exhibited anomalies of the eye, microphthalmia or anophthalmia.
effects.source_label: SCCS/1344/10, Opinion on Quaternium-15 (cis-isomer), section 3.3.8.2

conclusion.text: SCCS could not establish a reliable NOAEL or calculate a margin of safety, and it judges Quaternium-15's cis-isomer may not be safe for continued cosmetic use.
conclusion.quote: the SCCS considers its continued use in cosmetic products may not be safe for the consumers
conclusion.source_label: SCCS/1344/10, Opinion on Quaternium-15 (cis-isomer), section 4 Conclusion

limit.text: EU bans silver zinc zeolite generally as reprotoxic category 2 (Annex II, Reg. (EU) 2026/909, 28 April 2026), except up to 1% with silver capped at 2.5% in deodorant spray and powder foundation (Annex V).
limit.quote: the silver content in Ammonium Silver Zinc Aluminium Silicate must not exceed 2,5 %.
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex V export (entry 61) and Annex II export (entry 1597), citing Regulation (EU) 2026/909

basis_dose.text: SCCS references a rat two-generation study (Schroeder 2002) using oral gavage doses of 200, 700, and 2000 mg/kg bw/day; offspring heart enlargement, the finding used for developmental classification, appeared at the mid and high doses.
basis_dose.quote: performed with oral gavage doses of 200, 700, 2000 mg/kg bw/day in Rats (Schroeder 2002)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS/1650/23, Final Opinion on Silver Zinc Zeolite, section 3.4.5.1 Fertility and reproduction toxicity (dose levels; the heart-enlargement finding is discussed in the following section 3.4.5.2 Developmental Toxicity, citing the same study)

effects.text: In rats, silver zinc zeolite enlarged the heart in F2 pups at the mid dose and in F1 pups at the high dose, alongside maternal toxicity.
effects.quote: the enlargement of hearts reported at the mid dose in F2 pups (5/27 males and 4/26 females)
effects.source_label: SCCS/1650/23, Final Opinion on Silver Zinc Zeolite, section 3.4.5.2

conclusion.text: SCCS concludes silver zinc zeolite with up to 2.5% silver is safe at 1% in spray deodorant and powder foundation, with margins of safety of 109 to 3570 depending on exposure route.
conclusion.quote: The SCCS considers that Silver Zinc Zeolite (CAS No. 130328-20-0) incorporating a maximum silver content of 2.5% is safe in spray deodorant and powder foundation when used at the proposed concentration of 1%.
conclusion.source_label: SCCS/1650/23, Final Opinion on Silver Zinc Zeolite, section 4 Conclusion

limit.text: EU cosmetics law caps methanol at 5% of the ethanol/isopropyl alcohol content when used as a denaturant, per Annex III entry 52 of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 of 22 December 2009.
limit.quote: Denaturant for ethanol and isopropyl alcohol 5 % (as a % ethanol and isopropyl alcohol)
limit.source_label: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Annex III, entry 52 (OJ L 342, 22.12.2009)

conclusion.text: CIR's Expert Panel concluded methanol is safe for use as a denaturant in cosmetic alcohol and reaffirmed this conclusion in 2023 after reviewing newer toxicology data.
conclusion.quote: The Panel concluded that based on the data presented in the safety assessment, Methyl Alcohol is safe as used to denature alcohol used in cosmetic products.
conclusion.source_label: CIR Re-Review Summary, Methyl Alcohol (cir-safety.org)

limit.text: EU law allows Thiomersal and Phenylmercuric salts (including borate) only in eye products, at up to 0.007% calculated as mercury, combined if both are present.
limit.quote: Eye products 0,007 % (of Hg) If mixed with other mercurial compounds authorised by this Regulation, the maximum concentration of Hg remains fixed at 0,007 %
limit.source_label: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Annex V, entries 16 and 17; consolidated text CELEX 02009R1223-20250501, fetched directly from the EUR-Lex/Publications Office cellar (the CosIng CSV mirror shows stale 'Directive' wording for entry 17; the actual consolidated law reads 'Regulation' for both entries 16 and 17)

basis_dose.text: Lacking ethylmercury-specific developmental data, SCCS used methylmercury data in rats, where developmental immune effects occurred at a LOAEL of 0.0003-0.0006 mg Hg/kg bw/day.
basis_dose.quote: Developmental effects on the immune system have been noted with meHg in rat models with a LOAEL ranging from 0.0003 to 0.0006 Hg mg/kg bw/day, see also Table 3.4.4-1 above.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCS/1686/25, Scientific advice on the safety of Thiomersal and Phenylmercuric salts as preservatives in cosmetic products (final version)

effects.text: In voles, a single 0.125 mg/kg bw dose of phenylmercuric acetate given on gestation day 8 significantly increased pregnancy implantation loss, per the cited study.
effects.quote: Exposure [of Microtus ochrogaster in terms of a single intraperitoneal dose] to 0.125 mg/kg bw PMA at day 8 in the gestation caused significantly increased implantation loss.
effects.source_label: SCCS/1686/25, Scientific advice on the safety of Thiomersal and Phenylmercuric salts as preservatives in cosmetic products (final version)

conclusion.text: SCCS concluded the preservatives are not safe in cosmetic eye products at currently permitted levels, citing both a renal-toxicity margin of safety below 100 and unresolved genotoxicity evidence.
conclusion.quote: Considering that the Margin of Safety based on renal toxicity as the most sensitive endpoint is less than 100, and that genotoxicity evidence is unresolved, the use of 'Thiomersal' and 'Phenylmercuric salts'
conclusion.source_label: SCCS/1686/25, Scientific advice on the safety of Thiomersal and Phenylmercuric salts as preservatives in cosmetic products (final version)

Mercury and mercury compounds.documented_as: the mercury preservatives thiomersal and phenylmercuric salts

limit.text: Both substances are banned (Annex II), except the sulphate may stabilise hydrogen peroxide at up to 0.3% in rinse-off and 0.03% in leave-on hair products.
limit.quote: Stabilizer for hydrogen peroxide in rinse-off hair products Stabilizer for hydrogen peroxide in leave-on hair products (0,3 % as base) (0,03 % as base)
limit.source_label: Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, Annex II entry 395 and Annex III entry 51, as corrected by Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/1966

basis_dose.text: CIR's pending 2026 draft risk assessment uses a rabbit developmental-toxicity NOAEL of 5 mg/kg bw/day as its point of departure, though the Panel still calls this NOAEL data insufficient.
basis_dose.quote: Since the 5 mg/kg/day dose from the rabbit study was used as the point of departure in the risk assessment, please clearly state that this dose was a NOAEL in the Developmental and Reproductive Toxicity section
basis_dose.source_label: CIR, Draft Tentative Amended Report on Oxyquinoline and Oxyquinoline Sulfate

effects.text: In rabbits, the cited study found decreased live-born female offspring at 60 mg/kg bw/day and skeletal malformations from 15 mg/kg bw/day upward.
effects.quote: A decreased number of live-born female offspring (at 60 mg/kg bw/d) and skeletal malformations (at ≥ 15 mg/kg) were observed in a prenatal developmental toxicity assay
effects.source_label: CIR, Draft Tentative Amended Report on Oxyquinoline and Oxyquinoline Sulfate

conclusion.text: CIR's currently published Final Amended Report still concludes both ingredients are safe only as rinse-off hydrogen-peroxide stabilisers, with leave-on safety data judged insufficient.
conclusion.quote: The CIR Expert Panel concludes that Oxyquinoline and Oxyquinoline Sulfate are safe as used in stabilizers for hydrogen peroxide in rinse-off hair care products.
conclusion.source_label: CIR Final Amended Report on Oxyquinoline and Oxyquinoline Sulfate, issued June 2002 (no day of month stated in source), published 2006, as recapped in the 2026 Draft Tentative Amended Report

limit.text: Dibutyl phthalate has been banned from cosmetic products since Commission Directive 2004/93/EC, now carried as Annex II entry 675 of Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009.
limit.quote: 675. Dibutyl phthalate (Cas No 84-74-2)
limit.source_label: Commission Directive 2004/93/EC of 21 September 2004 amending Council Directive 76/768/EEC Annexes II and III, fetched directly from the EUR-Lex/Publications Office cellar; carried forward as Annex II entry 675 of the consolidated Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009, independently confirmed in that consolidated text

basis_dose.text: The EU risk assessment derived a developmental-toxicity LOAEL of 2 mg/kg bw/day in rats, since effects were still present at the lowest dose tested.
basis_dose.quote: A LOAEL of 2 mg/kg bw/d feed was derived, since the effects were reversible at all dose levels, particularly the lowest dose level (20 mg/kg feed, equivalent to 1.5 to 3 mg/kg bw/day)
basis_dose.source_label: SCCP/1016/06, Opinion on phthalates in cosmetic products (adopted 21 March 2007)

effects.text: In rats, DBP damages developing germ cells in the testis and produces anti-androgenic effects noted in foetuses, per the committee's summary.
effects.quote: In adult rats, the testis is the target. DBP and DEHP have effects on germ cell development/depletion, BBP affects epididymal spermatozoa concentration. Anti-androgenic effects have also been noted in foetal rats.
effects.source_label: SCCP/1016/06, Opinion on phthalates in cosmetic products (adopted 21 March 2007)

conclusion.text: CIR's Expert Panel reaffirmed in 2002, without reopening the 1985 Final Report, that DBP, DMP and DEP remain safe for cosmetic use at present practices and concentrations.
conclusion.quote: the CIR Expert Panel concludes that Dibutyl Phthalate, Dimethyl Phthalate, and Diethyl Phthalate are safe for use in cosmetic products in the present practices of use and concentration
conclusion.source_label: CIR Expert Panel meeting discussion of June 18-19, 2002 (reaffirming, with edited wording, the Panel's 1985 Final Report on Dibutyl, Dimethyl and Diethyl Phthalate), recapped in CIR's 2024 DBP re-review Strategy Memo

limit.text: Annex II entry 677 of the EU Cosmetics Regulation bans DEHP outright in cosmetic products, added by Commission Directive 2004/93/EC of 21 September 2004 implementing the CMR prohibition.
limit.quote: 677. bis(2-Ethylhexyl) phthalate (Cas No 117-81-7)
limit.source_label: Commission Directive 2004/93/EC, Annex, point 2 (OJ L 300, 25.9.2004, p. 13-41; entry 677 on p. L300/22)

basis_dose.text: The SCCP's 2007 phthalates opinion gives a NOAEL of 4.8 mg/kg bw/day for DEHP in rats, from a three-generation reproduction study (Wolfe et al. 2003), confirmed by CSTEE (2004b) and EFSA (2005d).
basis_dose.quote: NOAEL: 4.8 mg/kg/d based on testicular effects in a three generation guideline study (Wolfe et al, 2003, cited in DEHP RAR, 2003).
basis_dose.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007 (SCCP, direct predecessor of the SCCS)

effects.text: SCCP names testicular germ-cell effects in adult rats, alongside developmental toxicity, as DEHP's critical reproductive and developmental endpoint.
effects.quote: In adult rats, the testis is the target. DBP and DEHP have effects on germ cell development/depletion, BBP affects epididymal spermatozoa concentration.
effects.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007

conclusion.text: For DEHP traces found as perfume contaminants, SCCP calculates a margin of safety of 1920 and concludes traces up to 100 ppm pose no risk, though DEHP use itself remains banned under Annex II.
conclusion.quote: the SCCP is of the opinion that traces of up to 100 ppm total or per substance do not indicate a risk to the health of the consumer
conclusion.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007

limit.text: Annex II entry 1152 of the EU Cosmetics Regulation currently bans BBP (CAS 85-68-7) outright in cosmetic products as a Category 1B reproductive toxicant.
limit.source_label: CosIng Annex II export - List of substances prohibited in cosmetic products (European Commission, consolidated)

basis_dose.text: SCCP's 2007 phthalates opinion gives a NOAEL of 50 mg/kg bw/day for BBP in rats, based on reproductive effects (SCHER 2005, EFSA 2005f); CIR separately lists BBP as reviewed since 1992.
basis_dose.quote: NOAEL 50 reproductive effects
basis_dose.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007; corroborated by CIR's Quick Reference Table entry for Butyl Benzyl Phthalate (JACT 11(1):1-23, 1992; IJT 30(Suppl.2):73-127, 2011; IJT 36(Suppl 2):14-58, 2017)

effects.text: SCCP states BBP's reproductive effect is reduced epididymal spermatozoa concentration in adult rats, part of the broader phthalate testicular-effects pattern.
effects.quote: BBP affects epididymal spermatozoa concentration.
effects.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007

conclusion.text: SCCP includes BBP among phthalates whose perfume traces up to 100 ppm it finds pose no risk, citing a high margin of safety; CIR separately lists a 'Safe' finding for BBP in cosmetics.
conclusion.quote: the SCCP is of the opinion that traces of up to 100 ppm total or per substance do not indicate a risk to the health of the consumer
conclusion.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007; CIR Quick Reference Table lists Butyl Benzyl Phthalate finding 'S' (Safe)

limit.text: Annex II entry 1492 of the EU Cosmetics Regulation bans DIBP outright, added by Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/831 which entered into force 20 days after its 23 May 2019 OJ publication.
limit.quote: This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/831 of 22 May 2019, Article 2 (OJ L 137, 23.5.2019, p. 29)

basis_dose.text: SCCP's 2007 opinion reports that 600 mg/kg bw/day DIBP given to pregnant rats on gestation days 7-21 produced the developmental effects behind its reproductive-toxicity classification.
basis_dose.quote: If dosed at 600 mg/kg bw/day to pregnant rats on gestation days 7 –21, male offspring showed similar testicular and developmental effects as found with DBP and DEHP.
basis_dose.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007, citing Borch et al. 2006

effects.text: SCCP states DIBP-exposed male rat offspring showed testicular and developmental effects similar to those caused by DBP and DEHP, after maternal dosing in pregnancy.
effects.quote: male offspring showed similar testicular and developmental effects as found with DBP and DEHP
effects.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007

conclusion.text: SCCP concludes that the low DIBP concentrations found in perfume as unintentional contamination pose no measurable risk, without stating a numeric margin of safety for DIBP specifically.
conclusion.quote: The low concentrations of DIBP (0.2 - 38 mg/kg) found in samples of perfume suggest unintentional exposure from perfume and other cosmetics would pose no measurable risk for the consumer.
conclusion.source_label: SCCP Opinion SCCP/1016/06, 'Opinion on Phthalates in Cosmetic Products', adopted 21 March 2007

limit.text: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/1531 added MIBK (CAS 108-10-1) as entry 1689 to Annex II, the list of substances banned in cosmetic products, applying from 17 December 2022.
limit.quote: Article 1 shall apply from 17 December 2022.
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2022/1531, Publications Office cellar copy (EUR-Lex blocked by WAF challenge)

basis_dose.text: In a two-generation inhalation study in Sprague-Dawley rats, the NOAEL for reproductive endpoints was 2000 ppm, the highest concentration tested (reported as an inhalation concentration, not mg/kg bw/day).
basis_dose.quote: For reproductive endpoints, the highest concentration tested, 2000 ppm, was considered the no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL).
basis_dose.source_label: CIR, Amended Safety Assessment of MIBK as Used in Cosmetics (Draft Final Amended Report, Sept. 2024)

effects.text: In Fischer 344 rats, fetal body weight per litter was significantly reduced at both 300 ppm (about 97% of control, p<.05) and 3000 ppm (about 93-94% of control, p<.001), not at 1000 ppm.
effects.quote: Fetal body weight was slightly reduced at 300 ppm (≈97% of control values; p < .05), but not at 1000 ppm.
effects.source_label: CIR, Amended Safety Assessment of MIBK as Used in Cosmetics (citing Tyl et al. 1987)

conclusion.text: The CIR Expert Panel concluded that MIBK is safe as used in nail polish removers and as an alcohol denaturant in cosmetic products.
conclusion.quote: the CIR Expert Panel concludes that MIBK is safe as used in nail polish removers and as an alcohol denaturant in cosmetic products
conclusion.source_label: CIR, Amended Safety Assessment of MIBK as Used in Cosmetics

limit.text: Tetrahydrofurfuryl methacrylate (CAS 2455-24-5) does not appear in any entry of the EU Cosmetics Regulation's Annexes II-VI (prohibited, restricted, colorants, preservatives, or UV-filter lists) as exported from CosIng on 3 October 2026.
limit.quote: LIST OF SUBSTANCES PROHIBITED IN COSMETIC PRODUCTS
limit.source_label: CosIng (EU CosIng database), official annex CSV exports, Annexes II-VI (last updated 29/09/2026)

basis_dose.text: In a combined OECD TG 422 study in Sprague Dawley rats, the NOAEL for reproductive and developmental toxicity was 0.3 g/kg bw/day for males and 0.12 g/kg bw/day for females and their litters.
basis_dose.quote: The NOAEL for reproductive and developmental toxicity was considered to be 0.3 g/kg bw/d for males and 0.12 g/kg bw/d for females and their litters.
basis_dose.source_label: CIR, Safety Assessment of Methacrylate Ester Monomers as Used in Cosmetics (Re-Review, Nov. 2021)

effects.text: In Sprague Dawley rats, the high dose (0.3 g/kg bw/day) significantly increased pre-birth pup loss and prolonged gestation length, with missing or dead pups noted at that dose.
effects.quote: The pre-birth loss was significantly increased at statistical analysis, in high dose females.
effects.source_label: CIR, Safety Assessment of Methacrylate Ester Monomers as Used in Cosmetics (Re-Review, Nov. 2021)

conclusion.text: The CIR Expert Panel reaffirmed its 2005 conclusion that Tetrahydrofurfuryl Methacrylate is safe as used in nail enhancement products when skin contact is avoided, declining to reopen the assessment at its December 2021 meeting.
conclusion.quote: The Panel determined to not reopen this safety assessment on methacrylate ester monomers and reaffirmed the original conclusion.
conclusion.source_label: CIR, Rereview Summary: Methacrylate Ester Monomers, Admin materials for the 160th Expert Panel Meeting, March 7-8 2022 (recounting the December 2021 decision)

limit.text: Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/1490 added Pentetic Acid (CAS 67-43-6, entry 1720) and Pentasodium Pentetate (CAS 140-01-2, entry 1721) to Annex II, banning both from cosmetic products from 1 December 2023.
limit.quote: It shall apply from 1 December 2023.
limit.source_label: Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/1490, Publications Office cellar copy (EUR-Lex blocked by WAF challenge)
